title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos chain vicious strike into provoke, save doom shield for confirmed burst, pull adds with capture. beginner pve rotation chain vicious strike to build and hold threat. lock the primary target with provoke. time doom shield or other damage-reduction cooldowns specifically against confirmed incoming boss burst, rather than on cooldown. follow up locked-down or staggered targets with punishment and decisive strike for your hardest hits aion2hub, date unknown1 aoeah, 2025-112. multi-target pulls use capture to drag scattered adds into a cluster, then use trial (falling sword spirits) or shield strike to hit the whole pack at once. both scale their return, defense shred or healing, with the number of enemies hit single source (community synthesis, no direct link) aggro and defensive cooldowns mix provoke and what one source calls "god's punishment" alternately rather than spamming a single taunt; relying on one taunt skill is cited as a common way to lose aggro on mixed mob/boss pulls single source, unconfirmed skill name reserve big shields and damage-reduction cooldowns for confirmed mechanics, telegraphed boss bursts, instead of using them defensively on cooldown or reactively after damage has already landed single source no reliable source found documenting an auto-hunt or macro skill setup specifically for templar. gladiator sources document a macro setup; nothing equivalent turned up for templar. templar rotation combos pve aggro

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes templar levels at a moderate pace: tough and self-sufficient, but not a fast solo killer. solo comfort: strong self-sustain via lifesteal (bloodsword slash), shields that heal based on hits landed, and cc/pulls via capture make it survivable and good against larger mob groups trade-off: low personal damage next to gladiator, assassin, and sorcerer means clear speed and leveling pace can feel slow, especially with an unoptimized gear or skill setup pvpbank, date unknown1 sustain and mob density sustain comes primarily from damage-to-healing conversion, bloodsword slash heals 100% of damage dealt off flash cut procs, and shields that scale with enemies hit, not from potions or mana regen pvpbank, date unknown2 handles larger mob groups comfortably thanks to its aoe pull (capture) and multi-target defense and heal skills (trial, shield strike): "win through consistency and battlefield control rather than burst" pvpbank, date unknown3 when the class "turns on": sources consistently flag gear, mastery investment, and defensive-stat itemization as having an outsized impact on templar performance, more so than for most other classes. the class feels notably better once gear catches up rather than being strong purely from base kit pvpbank, date unknown4. templar leveling solo pve sustain

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes play actively, save cooldowns for real bursts, and do not expect gladiator-level clear speed. playing statically instead of actively repositioning; sources note the class rewards active tactical positioning and constant movement, not passive tanking single source. using big defensive cooldowns like doom shield reactively or on cooldown instead of saving them for confirmed, telegraphed boss burst windows single source. relying on a single taunt skill on mixed pulls instead of alternating taunts, cited as a cause of lost aggro single source. underestimating how gear, mastery, and defensive-stat dependent the class is, and under-investing in upgrades relative to other classes pvpbank, date unknown1. neglecting weapon upgrades in favor of armor only, when weapon level affects threat generation and the class's already-low dps. directional caution only, sourced from legacy aion 1 templar wiki content, not confirmed for aion 2 aion.fandom (aion 1)2. expecting gladiator, assassin, or sorcerer-level solo clear speed and getting frustrated, instead of leaning into the control and durability playstyle the class is built around pvpbank, date unknown3. not consolidating scattered mobs with capture before using aoe mitigation or heal skills, losing out on the healing-per-target-hit scaling those skills offer single source. skipping general new-player fundamentals: learning combat and movement before spending scarce upgrade materials applies to templar as much as any class aion2wiki, date unknown4. templar mistakes tips beginners

title: Overview and role
text: overview and role gladiator is a forgiving, self-sustaining melee dps that can flex into off-tank duty. the gladiator is aion 2's heavy melee dps with meaningful off-tank capability, wielding two-handed weapons: a greatsword or a polearm confirmed aion2hub, date unknown1 mmom, date unknown2. in korean the class is referred to as 검성, roughly "sword saint." korean community threads on title: Skill priority
text: skill priority two kr guides partly disagree; attack preparation is the one passive every source agrees is critical. two independent vortex gaming write-ups give partially overlapping, partially conflicting pve skill priorities. both are kr-era. priority order 1 do first: strike of ruin (specialized) then: charge strike, shatter wave, ankle cut, leap strike later: armor of balance, zikel's blessing, assault stance vortexgaming, date unknown1 priority order 2 do first: survival stance, called strong for both pvp and pve then: sharp separation (three specializations, or spirit/mp recovery if mana is tight), slam of severance (movement-skill change plus critical-hit mp recovery) then: leap strike (combat-readiness effect matters, recast reset useful for grinding), strike down (specialize for action-immune targets, guarantees a critical hit at skill level 20) then: crushing wave, recast reset on critical hit rated essential deprioritize: armor of protection and damage absorption, citing low efficiency from long recast times vortexgaming, date unknown2 core masteries (korean guidance) 예리한 일격 (sharp strike / keen strike): non-targeted, move-while-casting hit that builds threat and restores mp; level to 12 절단의 맹타 (cleaving fierce strike): aoe hit that raises threat and the groggy gauge; also level to 12 single source redwendy, date unknown3 passives attack preparation (공격 준비, raises attack power and defense): repeatedly called the single most important passive across both english and korean sources confirmed vortexgaming, date unknown4 redwendy, date unknown5 veteran counter: amplifies damage after a successful block; recommended to be maxed out single source vortexgaming, date unknown6 weakness analysis (약점 파악, raises critical hit rate and perfect stat) and blood absorption (피의 흡수, lifesteal on hit) round out the recommended passive set single source redwendy, date unknown7 skip and chain notes skills to ignore early: armor of protection and damage absorption per priority order 2 above; treat as single-source/contested since priority order 1 does not mention either skill. mastery/chain skills: strike down is a chain enabler against action-immune (staggered) targets and a guaranteed-crit finisher once specialized to level 20 single source vortexgaming, date unknown8. gladiator skill priority actives passives

title: Leveling build
text: leveling build max sharp strike, then push cleaving fierce strike to skill lv 12 before passives; zikel's blessing is the first stigma. this order comes from korean gladiator (검성) community threads on inven, corroborated by a kr blog inven, 2025-111 redwendy, date unknown2. every number below is the skill's own internal level (its 8/12/16/20/25 breakpoint), not your character level, unless a step says otherwise. skill point order stepwhenskilltake towhysrc 1from lv 1sharp strike (예리한 일격)maxkeeps sustain and mana up while grindinginven, 2025-11 2nextcleaving fierce strike (절단의 맹타)skill lv 12most recommended skill to push to 12 firstinven, 2025-11 redwendy, date unknown passives first: survival stance (생존 자세) inven, 2025-113 then: armor of protection (보호의 갑옷) inven, 2025-114 then max, in order: blood absorption (피의 흡수), attack preparation (공격 준비), weakness analysis (약점 파악) inven, 2025-115 redwendy, date unknown6 level by level lv 1-12max sharp strike, push cleaving fierce strike to skill lv 12, then dump into passivesthis leveling-phase order comes from inven's gladiator board, corroborated by redwendy's write-up inven, 2025-117 redwendy, date unknown8. lv 23stigma unlocks: slot zikel's blessing firstevery source that names a first-priority pve stigma names zikel's blessing (지켈의 축복) inven, date unknown9. see the note below before slotting a second. at caphand-off: push the pve core 3 to skill lv 20downward strike, cleaving fierce strike, and destruction slash become the mandatory endgame trio inven, date unknown10 inven, 2026-0211. to skill lv 16 downward strike (내려찍기) shatter wave (분쇄파동) cleaving fierce strike (절단의맹타) destruction slash (파멸의맹타) yurin's blade (유린의검) to skill lv 20 downward strike cleaving fierce strike destruction slash then shatter wave or yurin's blade, to taste both paths come from the same 2026-02-02 thread, the most detailed step order found for this class inven, 2026-0212; treat skill lv 20 as the target state to grow into once skill points are in surplus, not a leveling order. see skill priority above and stigma picks below for the rest of the endgame spread. no separate "leave at level 1" list: the only level-1 pick the note supports is fury wave, a stigma skill covered in the warning below. no "gear while leveling" block either, since the note found no reliable source for level-specific gear or weapon-swap breakpoints for this class. assault stance (돌격 자세) is called a fixed level-20 or level-25 stigma pick by three sources inven, 2026-0213, but a separate pve-focused thread excludes it entirely, calling it inferior to support-synergy picks inven, date unknown14. treat its pve value as contested, not confirmed. avoid: pushing fury wave (분노의 파동) past stigma level 1; title: Stigma picks
text: stigma picks max assault stance and zikel's blessing first; they repeat as top picks across every source. system basics stigmas unlock around level 23 greater stigma slots unlock via group quests around level 45 to 50 normal stigma skills cap at level 20 on base shards kr-era, subject to change at global launch the korean service has since raised the cap to 25, with up to six stigmas equippable at once expcarry, date unknown1 pve stigma set armor of balance, zikel's blessing, assault stance, block, path explosion enhancement priority: level path explosion to 15 (max 20 if resources allow), armor of balance to level 20 single source vortexgaming, date unknown2 alternate pve stigma set assault stance, zikel's blessing (called essential, +50% danite hit chance), focused block, blade wind, perseverance contested vortexgaming, date unknown3 pvp stigma set blade toss (mandatory, 40% healing reduction plus a 50% base effect), tenacity (3-second survival window), assault stance (also resets tenacity's cooldown), forced bind (combo enabler) single source vortexgaming, date unknown4 alternate pvp stigma set assault stance, armor of balance, blade wind, siege vortexgaming, date unknown5 korean community consensus: 지켈 (zikel's blessing) and 돌격 자세 (assault stance) are both worth maxing to stigma level 25 for pve and pvp alike, with assault stance as the top pick to invest in first; fill remaining slots to taste after that single source redwendy, date unknown6 inven, date unknown7. what to spend stigma shards on first: across every gladiator source, assault stance and zikel's blessing are the two names that repeat as first priority confirmed pattern, three independent sources, consistent with the general system advice to fund whatever you actually have equipped over situational alternates expcarry, date unknown8. gladiator stigma skills progression

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route no official gladiator route exists; community guidance says invest in active-skill nodes first. recommended node order (community synthesis, kr-era) single source, kr-era, community synthesis not an official guide community synthesis recommends investing in blue (active-skill-level) nodes first, starting from the board's start node (s) and pushing toward whichever aggressive dps-increasing nodes are reachable without breaking the connection chain miknk.co.kr, date unknown1. basic attack skill always-on skill conditional skill groggy skill early on, only the basic attack and always-on skill plus one need to be opened to play comfortably. a forum thread on nezekan-board point optimization for gladiator corroborates the "actives first" approach without adding new detail single source inven, date unknown2. how the board works daevanion points buy nodes on a shared board; nodes add either flat combat stats or extra levels to specific skills. points come from normal leveling plus daevanion crystals from quests and achievements. strategy: path to the nearest node that actually helps your loadout and treat filler connector nodes as a toll, not a destination. damage-focused builds like gladiator's should weight uptime and output nodes over pure survival nodes: "damage builds value uptime and output... tanks value control and survival" expcarry, date unknown3. kr-era reset costs 500 kinah per individual node in the korean client; cost may differ at global launch expcarry, date unknown4. no reliable source found on when specifically a gladiator should reset. gladiator daevanion board progression

title: Arcana
text: arcana no confirmed arcana list for gladiator; a chalice/parchment/compass/paper/mirror set is documented. recommended arcana types for gladiator/swordmaster: chalice, parchment, compass, paper, and mirror single source, search-synthesized vortexgaming, date unknown1. chalice: vitality chalice recommended, prioritize the strike down and crushing wave slots. parchment: strike down treated as essential, with slam of destruction and sharp strike as secondary picks. compass: slam of severance and crushing wave essential, followed by violate sword, dashing strike, sword aura tree, and impact release. paper: a mana-type paper is recommended for increased destructive power, paired with raising attack preparation. mirror: veteran counter and exploit weakness are the priority effects; the specific card name for mirror was not given in the source. for newer players building a general arcana set rather than min-maxing per skill, a frenzy 4 / purity 2 set is recommended, described as easier to build and giving strong early pve scaling into higher-level transcendence content single source mmoexp, date unknown2. arcana cards to avoid: two independent korean community threads warn against making a unique-grade arcana card out of 검기 난무 (sword aura rampage) or 파멸의 맹타 (ruin's fierce strike), calling it something players will regret; they instead insist the chalice (성배) card must be built around 내려찍기 (downward strike) kr-era single source per claim, two threads agree inven, date unknown3 fmkorea, date unknown4. separately, on the newer arcana set additions, the 수호 (guardian) and 불굴 (indomitable) sets are framed as pvp-oriented and 징벌 (punishment) as pve-oriented, implying a gladiator pve build should avoid over-investing in the guardian/indomitable sets kr-era single source vortexgaming, date unknown5. gladiator arcana cards

title: Gear and stat priority

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos open with assault stance, chain aoe into finishers, and save lifesteal skills for right after big hits. beginner pve rotation, synthesizing the two vortex gaming skill-priority lists: open with assault stance for the combat-speed and mp-cost buff. weave in sharp strike / 예리한 일격 periodically to keep mp topped up between bigger hits. lead with your aoe knockdown, charge strike, path explosion, or shatter wave depending on which build you're following, to group and stagger enemies. follow with single-target finishers, strike down, ankle cut, leap strike, on priority or action-immune targets. close with crushing wave once its recast has been reset by a critical hit confirmed pattern vortexgaming, date unknown1 vortexgaming, date unknown2. key chain combos: forced bind into downward strike as a pvp setup-into-burst combo, and path explosion (knockdown) into downward strike as an alternate opener when forced bind is unavailable. blade toss doubles as a farming or poke damage tool outside of combo windows single source vortexgaming, date unknown3. macro setup documented for auto-hunt or quick execution: a macro bound to blade of severance, with sharp strike, sword dance, path explosion, and downward strike all linked to a single left-click input for streamlined execution single source vortexgaming, date unknown4. defensive and utility cooldowns blood smash (or "lifestealing blade" in another source's naming) converts roughly 15% of damage dealt into hp. it's recommended as a reactive tool, used right after taking a big hit or during a burst trade rather than spammed on cooldown, since its value comes from timing, not uptime single source pvpbank, date unknown5. korean community advice reinforces this for aoe survival specifically: dropping 분쇄파동 (shatter/crushing wave) into the center of a mob cluster heals you sharply in proportion to how many enemies it hits, a panic-button sustain tool when surrounded single source inven, date unknown6. gladiator rotation combos pve macro

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes gladiator levels fast and safe: strong aoe clear plus lifesteal sustain, though early levels feel slow. solo leveling comfort: high. multiple independent sources describe gladiator as one of the most stable and forgiving melee classes to solo-level, citing consistent aoe clearing plus reliable lifesteal sustain confirmed u4n, date unknown1 u4gm, date unknown2. sustain is primarily lifesteal-based: the blood absorption passive plus active skills like blood smash/lifestealing blade convert a percentage of damage into hp, rather than relying on potions or mana regen. sustain scales with landing hits on multiple enemies at once, so positioning for cluster hits directly improves survivability confirmed, same sources. mob density tips: the class is explicitly built to wade into mob clusters and clear them with sweeping aoe while healing off the damage dealt; learning enemy spawn and movement patterns to strike during cluster moments is called out as the core solo-leveling skill for this class single source u4gm, date unknown3. kr-era, pre-launch feedback: early levels reportedly feel sluggish and low-impact based on focus-test feedback, but the class is consistently described as transforming in the mid-game once better animations, tighter combos, and cooldown mastery come online contested-but-consistent fextralife, date unknown4 mmoexp, date unknown5. later balance passes may have changed this. gladiator leveling solo pve sustain

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes learn to dodge, weave basic attacks for mp, and enhance your weapon before armor. assuming heavy armor lets you tank hits without needing to dodge; learning dodge timing is called out as one of the biggest power spikes a new gladiator player can unlock single source aion2wiki, date unknown1. poor mp management from spamming skills instead of weaving basic attacks and sharp strike (예리한 일격) to keep mana topped up confirmed, english and korean sources redwendy, date unknown2 inven, date unknown3. over-investing scarce upgrade materials into starting gear before learning core combat and movement fundamentals single source aion2wiki, date unknown4. not prioritizing the weapon slot for enhancement, when weapon level drives most of a dps class's damage output single source, same guide aion2wiki, date unknown5. spamming lifesteal skills (blood smash/lifestealing blade) on cooldown instead of saving them for immediately after a big hit or during a burst trade, which wastes their sustain value single source pvpbank, date unknown6. ignoring positioning for aoe cluster hits, not baiting or gathering mobs into cleave range before committing an aoe skill single source u4gm, date unknown7. neglecting the attack preparation and veteran counter passives, which multiple sources call the class's most important scaling passives, in favor of leveling only pvp reach/burst), then being surprised the weapon doesn't fit the playstyle single source u4gm, date unknown10. investing stigma shards evenly across many stigmas instead of maxing the two or three actually equipped first, diluting overall power expcarry, date unknown11. the two or three actually equipped are assault stance and zikel's blessing. inferred from the general stigma spend-priority title: Overview and role
text: overview and role assassin is a hard, high-ceiling melee striker: stealth in, burst from behind, then disengage. the assassin is a melee dps class wielding daggers, with dual-dagger as the core setup and sword or bow noted as secondary/off options by some guides fextralife, date unknown1 aion2hub, date unknown2. playstyle it plays as a hit-and-run striker: open from stealth with ambush or shadowstrike. unload a fast dagger combo, quick slice and flash slice, for back-attack burst. disengage or weave defensively with evasion stance. this phrasing appears near-verbatim across sources (confirmed) aion2hub, date unknown3. difficulty rated hard by at least one general beginner guide, which calls assassin "suited for experienced players who enjoy positioning" and "not recommended for new players due to their high skill floor" overgear, date unknown4. a separate class-explainer source calls assassin the class with the highest skill ceiling and an active melee combo game timesaver, date unknown5. confirmed by two independent sources that this is not a beginner-friendly class, so expect a learning curve around positioning and animation-canceling. pve standing (contested) top pve burst considered the best pve class for clearing content per early focus-group-test (fgt) player rankings, ahead of ranger aion2hub, date unknown6 weaker sustained parse gains more from a short pvp engagement than from standing on a boss for an extended damage test, implying weaker sustained pve parse damage relative to ranged casters exitlag, date unknown7 treat assassin as strong-to-top pve burst but not the most forgiving sustained-dps pick. pvp standing multiple sources describe assassin as a top-tier pvp class. "was the kr launch problem child, too strong. nerfs brought it back to earth. it's still top-tier pvp, just no longer unfair." kr-era ggwtb, date unknown8 strengths: heavy burst, stealth engages, gap closers. weaknesses: unforgiving punishment for bad openers, real melee risk. a season 2 balance pass reportedly buffed assassin further for both pve and pvp, improving its standing in new endgame dungeons and the abyss (same source, kr-era, subject to change before global launch) party demand: assassin falls under "damage" roles rather than the guaranteed party-demand roles held by templar/cleric/chanter-type support and tank classes. it is wanted for burst but is not an auto-invite the way support classes are ggwtb, date unknown9. who should pick it: players who enjoy tight positioning, animation-cancel timing, and a high-risk/high-reward melee duelist playstyle, and who accept a rougher early learning curve for a strong pvp ceiling and competitive-to-top pve burst. assassin overview role dps melee daggers

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route boards unlock through level 45; sources disagree whether there are 6 or 8 total. board count (contested) the daevanion board unlocks progressively by level. one wiki source lists six boards: nezekan (lv 12), zikel (lv 20), vaizel (lv 30), triniel (lv 40), ariel (lv 45), azphel (lv 45) fextralife, date unknown1 a separate search summary additionally names marchutan and yustiel as advanced level-45 boards, for eight total fextralife, date unknown2 sources disagree on whether there are 6 or 8 total boards, possibly a page update or a kr/tw-versus-global difference. node types: grey nodes are stat increases (lowest point cost), green nodes level up passive skills, blue nodes level up active skills, and orange/unique nodes grant special effects (highest point cost) fextralife, date unknown3. this matches the blue-active/green-passive framing used elsewhere in this guide (confirmed). lv 12nezekan board unlocksrecommended route: prioritize hitting skill-level breakpoints (12/16/20) over the cheapest tile; ignore point-cost order when a lower-rarity tile completes a breakpoint field manual, date unknown4 (single source). post-breakpointsstat-node orderattack, then critical hit/accuracy, then hp, then defense (single source). points and farming daevanion points are earned through general progression and account/character milestones. no aion 2-specific source gave a precise farming list beyond "you will eventually get enough daevanion points to cover the entirety of the boards" fextralife, date unknown5. post-45 progression involves collecting lord-trace skill points and farming daevanion points from sealed/endgame content field manual, date unknown6 (single source). reset cost kr-era, single source, flagged by the source itself as provisional the only concrete reset cost figure found is a cross-class one, not confirmed assassin-specific: a korean patch reportedly set individual daevanion node resets to 500 kinah, with the client also supporting a full board reset. a dependency rule applies: a node cannot be removed if another already-acquired node depends on it. the source explicitly warns the number could change for global expcarry, date unknown7. when to reset, and whether 500 kinah is assassin-specific: no reliable source found. a korean search on "살성 데바니온 초기화 비용" (assassin daevanion reset cost) turns up only general discussion of counting activated nodes to estimate total daevanion crystal needs before a reset, with no assassin-specific cost figure contested/unclear fmkorea, date unknown8. net: reset cost is likely the same 500 kinah per node cross-class figure, but no second source confirms it is assassin-specific or unchanged, treat as unconfirmed for assassin specifically. assassin daevanion board nodes route

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes assassin levels well once breakpoint skills land around level 20, but needs careful positioning. solo leveling comfort: sources agree assassin can level efficiently once its early breakpoint skills (level 16/20 traits) are secured, but is not considered the most beginner-forgiving class due to its reliance on positioning overgear, date unknown1 overgear, date unknown2. sustain: pve-focused guides recommend prioritizing mana recovery and lifesteal-adjacent stigma/skill options during leveling to reduce downtime between pulls pvpbank, date unknown3. mob density and leveling phases one fan-made source splits leveling into two phases: before level 45: follow main story and orange quest objectives after level 45: shift to collecting lord-trace skill points and farming daevanion points from sealed/endgame content field manual, date unknown4 (single source) weekly loop: wanted order quests, abyss accessories, expedition gear, and transcendence arcana. when the class "turns on": no source gave an exact level, but the recurring theme across guides is that assassin's core identity (rear-attack multipliers, illusive clone plus triniel's dagger buff-chaining) only comes online once its level-20-ish core skills and matching stigmas are unlocked, implying a slower start than simpler classes. synthesized from multiple sources above, not a direct quote. assassin leveling solo sustain mob density

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes time stealth right before engaging, always attack from behind, and swap builds for pve vs pvp. poor stealth timing, entering stealth too early wastes its duration; it should be used right before the opening attack pvpbank, date unknown1. ignoring positioning, most of the class's damage multipliers require back attacks, so failing to reposition constantly caps your dps pvpbank, date unknown2. misusing rune/insignia stacking, detonating stacks with pattern explosion at the wrong stack count instead of at full stacks is called out as a major dps loss pvpbank, date unknown3. using the same build/stigma setup for both pve and pvp instead of swapping loadouts pvpbank, date unknown4. spreading skill points evenly across all abilities instead of committing to level 16/20 breakpoint skills first field manual, date unknown5. over-investing in gear that will be replaced almost immediately, instead of pacing enhancement spend to milestone gear u4gm, date unknown6 (could not verify by direct fetch, 403, single source). chasing a "perfect" meta build in the first 40 levels instead of just leveling with the core kit pvpbank, date unknown7. holding triniel's dagger too long, breaking buff-window alignment with your core attack chain, instead of using it in the recommended 3-8 second window field manual, date unknown8 (single source). letting illusive clone/swift contract cooldowns drift out of sync instead of chaining them together at the start of a damage window field manual, date unknown9 (single source). dropping defensive tools (evasion stance) too early in a fight, leaving no answer for incoming burst since assassin has low innate durability, "fragility and short reach" per the class overview aion2hub, date unknown10 field manual, date unknown11. assassin common mistakes beginner errors

title: Overview and role
text: overview and role ranger is a kiting ranged dps with a bow, easy to pick up, and a safe, strong choice for solo play and pve damage. role and playstyle bow is the main weapon; build examples also show an off-hand "guard" item alongside it aion2hub, date unknown1 aion2hub, date unknown2 playstyle is "a mobile, kiting ranged dps: lead with a high-damage snipe, maintain pressure with rapid fire and arrow skills," using distance and repositioning to avoid melee entirely aion2hub, date unknown3 47 total skills: 37 active, 10 passive (single source) difficulty rated easy-medium, "ideal for safe solo gameplay and mobile combat" and one of the more accessible damage options for new players overgear, date unknown4 a separate source calls ranger "a physical damage class that can kite and stay safe... a safe ranged damage option" for beginners timesaver, date unknown5 confirmed across two independent sources: ranger is friendlier for a new player than assassin. pve and pvp standing one title: Stigma picks
text: stigma picks rangers get 5 stigma slots from 13 total stigma skills; pve and pvp setups use different skills entirely. rangers have 11 active skills and 13 stigma skills total, but can only slot 5 at once (single source for the exact numbers; video content itself could not be fetched directly, title/description only) youtube, date unknown1. pve stigma branches: gale (attack-speed buff uptime), snipe (long-range opener amplification), rapid fire (filler damage) u4n, date unknown2 season 3-era skill-level framing: push byzel, blessed bow, and gryphon's arrow to level 20, keep supporting fire at 15 vortex gaming, date unknown3 kr-era contested/unclear whether "byzel," "blessed bow," and "gryphon's arrow" are stigma skills or daevanion-board active-skill nodes; the source's phrasing does not make this fully clear, so treat the mapping with caution. u4n naming not corroborated: other sources (ten ton hammer's ranger stigma list, aoeah's dps build roundup, a gameforge eu ranger pve/pvp thread) do not use u4n's gale/snipe/rapid fire terms, and the closest kr match found uses different names entirely (bow of blessing, griffon arrow, power of vaizel, supporting fire, see the level 45 set below). treat u4n's framing as likely its own fan-name shorthand rather than a corroborated branch structure single source, unresolved naming mismatch. pve vs pvp split confirmed via two independent kr threads: pve favors 축복의 칼날 (blade of blessing), 폭발하는 칼날 (exploding blade), 화살 폭풍 (arrow storm), and either 기습 차기 (ambush kick) or 바이드 (void); pvp favors 기습 차기 plus stealth skills, and a "purity" (순수) stat/skill setup even for players who only dabble in pvp kr-era fmkorea, date unknown4 inven, date unknown5. pve means damage maximization, pvp means survival/ambush focus, per the stated framing. level 45 advanced stigma bow of blessing (축복의 활): +7% smite during its duration, stacks with a chanter's party smite buff, mandatory griffon arrow (그리폰 화살): reportedly ~10% of total dps share, also mandatory power of vaizel (바이젤의 권능): 50% chance on crit to reduce all cooldowns by 1 second supporting fire (지원 사격): flat attack power increase leveling priority is bow of blessing and power of vaizel first single source kr-era vortexgaming, date unknown6. what to spend stigma shards on first: no reliable source found with an explicit "spend shards on x first" statement for ranger, unlike assassin, where multiple sources named illusive clone as the top shard priority. closest guidance: the branch priority above (gale, then snipe, then rapid fire, inferred from listing order, not an explicit statement), or by leveling order for the level 45 set: bow of blessing and power of vaizel first. ranger stigma shards gale snipe rapid fire

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route boards unlock every 10 levels from 12 to 45; put stat points into smite first, then critical hit, then attack. board unlocks nezekan (level 12), zikel (level 20), vaizel (level 30), triniel (level 40), ariel (level 45), azphel (level 45) fextralife, date unknown1 a separate search summary names eight total boards, adding marchutan and yustiel as additional level 45 advanced boards (date unknown) unclear if this is a page-version difference or a kr/tw-versus-global discrepancy, flagging both. node types class-agnostic, applies to ranger the same as assassin: grey = stat increase (1 point), green = passive skill level-up (2 points), blue = active skill level-up (3 points), orange/unique = special node (4 points) fextralife, date unknown2. this matches the blue-active/green-passive framing used elsewhere in this guide (confirmed). stat-node order (single source, no independent corroboration): smite first, targeting 60%+ on helmet, cloak, and other key gear pieces then critical hit, to maximize back-attack/critical damage output then attack and attack speed, to synergize with buff windows then accuracy, to avoid misses in endgame pve, with hp and defense as secondary, pvp-leaning priorities u4n, date unknown3 no ranger-specific source directly compares blue active-skill nodes, green passive nodes, and stat nodes, or which to prioritize first; the closest is the stat-node order above. no reliable source found comparing active-skill-nodes-first versus stat-nodes-first for ranger the way the assassin field manual did for assassin. when to reset: no reliable source found for ranger specifically. points sources: same general mechanism as assassin, progression-based accumulation. no ranger-specific farming guidance found beyond "you will eventually get enough daevanion points to cover the entirety of the boards" fextralife, date unknown4. ranger daevanion board nodes route

"vigor 4 / purity 4" is called one of the strongest long-term arcana configurations currently available vortex gaming, date unknown3 kr-era. ranger-specific picks active-skill level-20 targets: 속사 (rapid shot), 저격 (snipe), 송곳화살 (piercing arrow), 조준화살 (aimed shot) scales (천칭) card: pick one of five available skills, often snipe, freeing that skill from another arcana slot, plus a secondary option like "집중의 눈" (eye of focus/focus stat) if an evasion-stat build isn't feasible, a "공명치" (resonance/hp-and-resist) stat setup is a fallback weapon and guard arcana slots should fix combat speed and weapon-damage amplification first, then flex the remainder toward power, accuracy, or multi-hit single source kr-era inven, date unknown4 inven, date unknown5 ranger arcana cards transcendence

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos open with griffin arrow, apply marking arrow, then spam piercing arrow while repositioning constantly. beginner pve rotation single source: pvpbank, date unknown1 open with griffin arrow, a straight-line, high-burst opener with a long cooldown apply marking arrow, a debuff reducing enemy crit resistance and adding knockback spam piercing arrow mixed with basic shots; it has mp-recovery/lifesteal specialization options for sustained damage deploy arrow rain on cooldown, an aoe hitting up to six targets with a brief stun pvp approach emphasizes burst-and-cc chaining: enter from stealth, use silence arrow to shut down the opponent's actions, and use terrain/positioning control rather than a fixed combo string pvpbank, date unknown2. key playstyle principle: "motion is your main defense." rangers succeed through constant repositioning rather than tanking hits, requiring map awareness and cooldown management pvpbank, date unknown3. a separate source echoes "keep moving to avoid being targeted" and warns damage windows are short, recommending daevanion nodes to widen burst windows u4n, date unknown4. auto-hunt/macro setup is one of the better-documented areas for ranger specifically. a youtube guide title confirms it covers macro setup for skills, stigmas, and the daevanion board, though the video's actual content could not be retrieved, only youtube's generic footer returned youtube, date unknown5. a related written guide describes the macro setup as centered on four inputs (left click, right click, "3," "2"), and states developers have officially confirmed macros are permitted for aiming for high scores in dungeons, with stigma skills also groupable into a macro via a "turbo" function medium, date unknown6 (http 403 on direct fetch, search-summary-derived only, single source, unverified in full). defensive/utility cooldowns: no reliable source found naming a specific ranger defensive cooldown by name, unlike assassin's evasion stance/shadow walk. guidance is limited to the general "keep moving"/positioning principle above rather than a named skill. ranger rotation combo pve pvp opener

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes ranger levels comfortably solo thanks to kiting, but high ping can break its skill timing. solo leveling comfort: ranger is repeatedly described as comfortable and safe to solo-level, benefiting from ranged kiting and not needing to tank hits overgear, date unknown1 timesaver, date unknown2. confirmed across 2+ sources. sustain: mp recovery is named as a secondary stat priority "for sustained fights," and piercing arrow has lifesteal/mp-recovery specialization options useful for extended pulls pvpbank, date unknown3. mob density/turn-on point: no reliable source found giving a specific level at which ranger "turns on." the closest indirect signal is the stigma/skill guidance to hit byzel, blessed bow, and gryphon's arrow at level 20, suggesting the core kit solidifies around that point, similar to assassin's level 16-20 breakpoints. inferred, not explicitly stated vortex gaming, date unknown4 kr-era. latency sensitivity: one tier-list-adjacent source specifically warns that high ping causes intermittent skill release and reduces damage efficiency for ranger, worth flagging for a class that leans on precise skill weaving leprestore, date unknown5 (lower-trust marketing/tier-list site, single source). ranger leveling solo sustain latency

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes most ranger mistakes come from standing still, poor cooldown timing, and skipping accuracy investment. standing still in combat instead of continuously repositioning ("motion is your main defense") pvpbank, date unknown1 u4n, date unknown2 poor cooldown management, letting short damage windows go unused u4n, date unknown3 suboptimal gear synergy, not aligning daevanion nodes and gear stats to widen burst windows u4n, date unknown4 inadequate positioning in pvp specifically, getting caught out of range of escape tools u4n, date unknown5 ignoring accuracy investment, leading to avoidable misses in endgame pve content u4n, date unknown6 playing on high-latency connections without accounting for intermittent skill release, which reduces effective damage output leprestore, date unknown7 (single source, lower-trust) chasing "meta" builds or perfect gear too early instead of leveling with the recommended core skill/stigma branches (gale/snipe/rapid fire) fewer ranger-specific common-mistakes items exist than for assassin. items 1-5 above are directly sourced, item 6 is single-source, and item 7 is a general beginner-mistake pattern seen across aion 2 guides broadly, not ranger-specific in its original source, applied here by extension and flagged as inference rather than a documented claim. ranger common mistakes beginner errors

title: Overview and role
text: overview and role sorcerer is a glass-cannon ranged mage: huge burst and aoe, very low hp, and the steepest learning curve in the game. role and playstyle ranged magic damage dealer wielding a spellbook, built around fire and ice magic aion2hub.com, date unknown1 aion2boost.com, 2026-082 consistently described as a "glass cannon nuker": very high burst and aoe damage combined with very low hp and defense fextralife.com, 2026-023 gamesolusi.com, 2026-074 difficulty is rated at the top of the roster. one difficulty-focused tier list places sorcerer in s-tier (hardest), right beside assassin, citing extremely low survivability, unforgiving positioning requirements, and a high skill ceiling with almost no forgiveness for mistakes single source mmoexp.com, 2026-075. contested pve vs pvp ranking aion2boost.com framing pve grade: a, "with a real claim on higher" pvp grade: b, limited by survivability in extended trades aion2boost.com, 2026-086 leaderboard-data tier list pve grade: c-tier, only 83 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots argues the class "wants to stand still and cast" while harder encounters demand movement allthings.how, 2026-087 these two rankings genuinely disagree. aion2boost.com is a marketing/boosting site grading on theoretical ceiling; allthings.how claims to use actual leaderboard participation data. both are pre-launch, single-source assessments, treat the true pve standing as unsettled until global launch data exists. party demand: sorcerer is generally cited as a top-tier aoe and single-target burst dps with strong cc utility for parties, but its fragility means it depends heavily on positioning support and boss mechanic knowledge youtube.com, date unknown8. who should pick it: players who enjoy planning burst windows, are comfortable with high-risk, high-reward positioning, and are willing to relearn spell timing rather than face-tank mistakes. not for beginners: sorcerer is not a "forgiving" first class. spiritmaster or a melee class is an easier on-ramp by comparison. sorcerer overview role dps difficulty tier

global launch cap for this system is not yet confirmed expcarry.com, 2026-093. the same march 25, 2026 patch added a brand-new sorcerer-specific stigma called "hibernation," alongside buffs making "lumiel's space" into an aoe skill and a +20% damage increase to "hellfire" kr-era, balance may change aion2hub.com, 2026-034. a lower-trust build guide lists early stigma tiers as: tier 1 = "steel barrier" (a shield) and "improvement of elements"; tier 2 = "divine explosion" and "firewall" single source, low trust slashingcreeps.com, 2025-115. build philosophy (aion2boost.com) area pages deepen the multi-target engine and mana economy single-target pages fund burst alignment pvp pages spend real slots on escape tools and anti-melee defense rather than pure damage pve stigma priority: damage amplification first, control second, survivability third. pvp priority: escape/anti-melee first, control second, burst third aion2boost.com, 2026-086. a sorcerer-specific pve stigma investment order was also found: 원소강화 (elemental enhancement) first, 불의장벽 (fire wall) second, 지연폭발 (delayed explosion) third, then 강철보호막 (steel shield) fourth kr-era single source (exact source url not individually isolated from a multi-result search synthesis, treat as an unconfirmed community claim, date unknown). gap remains: no reliable source found for a specific recommended stigma loadout naming exact global skill ids, or for what to spend stigma shards on first beyond the general "fund frequently-used stigmas" progression order expcarry.com, 2026-097. sorcerer stigma picks build slots

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route shared cross-class board unlocking at 12; prioritize blue active-skill nodes early, with ice-vs-fire routing differing by spec. the daevanion board is a shared system across all classes, not sorcerer-specific, but the mechanics matter for build planning. it unlocks at level 12 aion2hub.com, 2026-061. node types and costs: grey = stat nodes (1 daevanion point), green = passive skill level-ups (2 points), blue = active skill level-ups (3 points), orange = unique specialty nodes at the board periphery granting bonuses like cooldown reduction or critical damage (4 points) fextralife.com, 2026-012. lv 12nezekancombat speed / cooldown reduction focus. fextralife.com, 2026-013 lv 20zikeldamage boost / tolerance. lv 30vaizelcritical damage / tolerance. lv 40trinielmulti-hit chance / resist. lv 45ariel and azphel (advanced)ariel is pve damage/tolerance, azphel is pvp damage/tolerance. two more advanced boards, marchutan and yustiel, are referenced elsewhere as also unlocking at 45 single source for naming. recommended early route (general, not sorcerer-specific): prioritize blue (active skill) nodes early to maximize immediate combat power, since nodes must be unlocked sequentially outward from the board's center and route choice matters as much as the final destination. aion2boost.com's sorcerer-specific framing: for pve, invest cooldown reduction and skill-potency nodes; area-focused players should lean into multi-target support nodes, single-target/burst players into burst-alignment nodes marketing source aion2boost.com, 2026-084. reset mechanics: korean live service currently offers free resets for mastery skills and stigmas; daevanion individual-node resets cost 500 kinah on kr live, but global costs are unconfirmed kr-era expcarry.com, 2026-095. a kr community source adds general (not node-specific) routing guidance: prioritize skill-level and corner (bonus) nodes first, then required passives, then remaining attack-stat options kr-era single source inven.co.kr, date unknown6. early routing reportedly differs depending on whether a sorcerer specializes into ice or fire, since the split is core to the class's kit, with community threads discussing a separate "early ice daevanion tree" build. gap remains: no sorcerer-specific node-by-node daevanion route (exact nodes in order) has been found. closest available guidance is the general "prioritize blue nodes early" advice, aion2boost's pve framing above, and the ice-vs-fire specialization routing note just above. sorcerer daevanion board route nodes

title: Arcana
text: arcana fill arcana slots immediately with usable cards rather than waiting for perfect drops, then focus training arcana on keepers. arcana is a shared cross-class system. current kr/tw arcana slot types include the original five (chalice, parchment, compass, bell, mirror) plus scales, key, hourglass, dice, and lantern kr-era, balance may change expcarry.com, 2026-091. cards come in common, rare, epic, and unique grades; general advice is to fill empty slots immediately with usable lower-grade cards rather than waiting for perfect drops, since even a lower-grade card provides item level, stats, set progress, and skill levels. leveling arcana uses training arcana consumables (kr/tw values: lesser 200 exp, intermediate 600, superior 1,500, ultimate 3,000); use training arcana only on cards you intend to keep rather than spreading it across filler cards. for dps classes generally, sorcerer included, the guidance is to prioritize cards that increase levels on the active skills and passives driving your main rotation, then complete damage-oriented set bonuses expcarry.com, 2026-092. check individual skill breakpoints, particularly around skill levels 16 to 20, rather than assume a universal formula. avoid: spreading training arcana across cards you do not plan to keep. sorcerer-specific slot picks (single kr guide) chalice and parchment: prioritize flaming burst and flaming arrow stats compass: wind of regret (호한의 바람), explicitly not flame barrage bell: mark of flame, cold summoning, and contract of rebirth mirror: fiery robes, life drain, and spirit absorption these english names are informal translations of kr terms from a single guide and are not confirmed official localizations kr-era single source, fan-translated names vortexgaming.io, date unknown3. this slotting order is single-source and kr-era, not independently corroborated. treat exact card and skill names as provisional until a second source or global localization confirms them. sorcerer arcana cards transcendence

title: Gear and stat priority
text: gear and stat priority spellbook and cloth armor are fixed; put intelligence and magic attack first, then cooldown reduction. weapon: spellbook (confirmed across all sources). armor type: cloth, standard for the class u4gm.com, date unknown1. two build paths recur across sources (confirmed pattern, single source on the exact stat lists): max burst (fire path) prioritizes critical hit, accuracy, and attack% for maximum single-target/aoe burst one source names "white dragon lord tome" as a recommended weapon single source, unverifiable u4n.com, 2026-012 control / kiting (ice path) prioritizes crowd control uptime and mobility aimed at pvp and solo challenging pve same source as max burst general stat priority (compiled) do first: intelligence and magic attack as primary offensive stats over physical defense then: cooldown reduction, called "essential" via daevanion allocation later / optional: critical hits, accuracy, life stats a separate guide's blunt framing: "aim for the skills to be achieved at level 16 and attack, critical hits and life last," implying skill-level breakpoints matter more early than raw stat itemization slashingcreeps.com, 2025-113. manastone/godstone-equivalent system (shared, not sorcerer-specific): gear has 2 to 4 randomly generated sockets; manastones slot into weapons/armor and spiritstones into accessories, with sockets often needing to be unlocked via manastone fasteners from gear extraction kr-era vortexgaming.io, date unknown4. godstones can be socketed onto enchanted items for extra combat effects and can be reset via "soul imprinting." one methodology guide explicitly declined to give stat priority, cautioning that "actual skill details require checking the live client" rather than trusting pre-launch numbers aion2kina.com, date unknown5. enhancement order cross-class general guidance: weapon first, then the guard/chest piece and accessories kr-era single source, general not sorcerer-exclusive lifefin.co.kr, date unknown6. remaining armor pieces (gloves, body, boots) are enhanced steadily for long-term use starting mid-progression. the same source separately flags daevanion, the amulet of revelation, and the belt of nobility as the three biggest early item-level gains to prioritize. gap remains: no reliable source found naming the specific manastone/godstone options a sorcerer should chase, or confirmed sorcerer set-effect bonuses. general cross-guide advice: raise core damage-skill levels via gear, daevanion, and arcana before chasing pure stat lines. sorcerer gear stat priority weapon armor

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos freeze with ice skills, then dump your highest-damage fire spells into the cc window. the most consistent mechanical description across sources is a freeze-then-burst (ice into fire) pattern: use ice skills to slow, freeze, or root a target so it cannot close distance or escape, then align your highest-damage fire spells during that cc window u4n.com, 2026-011. this is reinforced by the wiki's cool down/ice break/hellfire interactions, where cool down freezes for 3 seconds and can reset glacier strike's cooldown, and ice break deals bonus damage to frozen targets while resetting cool down on a critical hit, describing a genuine freeze-lock combo loop kr-era, in-progress build fextralife.com, 2026-022. beginner pve rotation use a defensive shield stigma proactively open trash packs with aoe spells for grouping and aggro (one source calls this skill "glacial wind" for aggro control) transition to single-target burst skills for tougher enemies and bosses slashingcreeps.com, 2025-113 macro/auto-hunt setup one korean-sourced guide, translated names, contested confidence: bind priority skills (translated "soothing wind," "winter's rest," "hellfire," "concentration") to a shared macro key use manually-controlled skills first (translated "elemental reinforcement," "wall of fire," "frost storm") before triggering the macro alternate left/right click basic attacks smoothly to cancel animations flags that a live balance patch changed right-click ice chain attack speed, requiring a skill-speed adjustment kr-era vortexgaming.io, date unknown4 defensive/utility cooldowns: mobility tools (referred to as "blink" in one source) are used to disengage from melee threats like assassins u4n.com, 2026-015. "the wisdom of lumiere," which halves mp cost of all skills for 10 seconds, is named as a burst-window enabler in the wiki skill list fextralife.com, 2026-026. no pet/spirit management applies to sorcerer, it is not a summoner class. sorcerer rotation combos freeze burst macro

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes pull to your control budget, not your damage; the class turns on once its aoe/cc engine comes online around level 16. solo leveling comfort is rated lower than average due to fragility: guides repeatedly stress "pull to your control budget, not your damage" as a core leveling habit, since the packs you can lock down with cc are the packs you can safely clear aion2boost.com, 2026-081. sustain is weak; the class has no core self-heal beyond shields and burst kill speed, so early levels require "fragile, methodical play," per aion2boost.com, until the area-damage engine comes online mid-progression for faster pack-clearing. beginner tip: treat positioning, not a stat, as your primary defensive tool. avoid pulling beyond your control capacity. when the class "turns on": sources agree the aoe/cc engine strengthens noticeably in the mid-teens once firestorm/hellfire-tier skills and their daevanion nodes are online, roughly the level-16 gate referenced by multiple guides slashingcreeps.com, 2025-112. this is corroborated by a layered framework recommending players first lock in safe positioning and cancellation mechanics before layering in damage output. sorcerer leveling notes solo mob density

title: Overview and role
text: overview and role spiritmaster is a pet-based ranged mage: safer and more forgiving than sorcerer, but its rotation is deeper than it looks. role and playstyle ranged magic damage dealer wielding an orb, built around summoning and rotating four elemental spirits (fire, water, wind, earth) aion2hub.com, date unknown1 fextralife.com, 2026-022 stacks damage-over-time effects, debuffs, and fear-based crowd control from range while the spirits act as semi-autonomous, turret-like damage sources rather than a single persistent pet aion2hub.com, date unknown3 difficulty rated notably lower than sorcerer: a difficulty-focused tier list places spiritmaster (referred to there as "spiritmaster/elementalist") in its most beginner-friendly bracket, citing "more safety tools than sorcerer" and a more forgiving learning curve while still delivering respectable damage single source mmoexp.com, 2026-074. other guides stress the rotation itself is deceptively demanding: many new players pick it up expecting a simple pet class, then get overwhelmed by the rotation, with the real skill expressed through spirit-cycle management, not simple button-pressing search-summary only, source 403'd exitlag.com, date unknown5. contested pve vs pvp ranking aion2boost.com framing pve grade: c, "burst is the roster's floor" pvp grade: c, vulnerable to any mechanic that neutralizes summons praises latency tolerance: "summons keep fighting through lag that cripples every reaction-based kit" aion2boost.com, 2026-086 leaderboard-data tier list pve grade: d-tier, the lowest of any class, only 34 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots concludes it "asks the most and returns the least in the current pve meta" allthings.how, 2026-087 leprestore.com framing claims spiritmaster is "the best current pve dps recommendation" claims an a-tier rating as "the biggest winner of pre-launch balance passes" search-summary only, direct fetch returned http 403, unverified against original text leprestore.com, date unknown these three assessments genuinely conflict, from a d-tier "asks the most, returns the least" verdict to an a-tier "biggest winner" claim. treat spiritmaster's pve ranking as unsettled rather than settled. its pvp framing is more consistent: sources agree it offers safer, more controlled ranged pressure than melee classes, with strong 1v1 utility from pet pressure plus fear-based crowd control aion2boost.com, 2026-088 pvpbank.com, date unknown9. party demand: cited as strong for sustained pressure and solo self-sufficiency but more mechanically demanding in group content where boss movement can disrupt spirit positioning aion2hub.com, date unknown10. who should pick it: players who want a self-sufficient solo class with built-in "pet tank" survivability and are willing to learn spirit-cycle management rather than a simple rotation. a reasonable beginner-friendly pick relative to sorcerer, but not a truly "easy" class once the rotation depth is considered. spiritmaster overview role dps pet difficulty tier

title: Skill priority
text: skill priority both major guides agree spirit strike is the top passive; everything else uses different fan-translated names. two independent guides give partially conflicting skill names for what appears to be the same core kit; both are reported here (contested naming, single source each for specific priority order). guide a (mmoexp, "warala" mechanic) recommends a "three spirit warala" setup using fire, water, and earth spirits, explicitly stating that adding a fourth, wind spirit, "slows down the rotation and lowers overall damage efficiency." do first: cold shock (lifesteal/survival), flame transfer (strong damage), a mobility specialization (called essential) then: ancient spirit (critical timing-dependent), elemental fusion (damage and instant-trigger chance) later / optional: fire spirit as primary summon, water spirit secondary, earth spirit situational passive priority: spirit strike and focus (direct damage) first, then spirit regeneration (resource recovery for ancient spirit). single source, spelling unconfirmed mmoexp.com, 2026-071 guide b (vortex gaming) recommends investing in only 4 active skills up to level 20 while emphasizing passive development. "flame incineration" gets maximum investment (20+) as primary damage dealer, with "frost shock," "elemental fusion," "curse," and "spatial domination" assigned to macro/mouse buttons. passive priority: 1) spirit strike, 2) concentration, 3) spirit revival. single source, machine/fan-translated vortexgaming.io, date unknown2 both guides agree "spirit strike" is the top passive skill priority confirmed across 2 sources. "elemental fusion" is described by both as a proc/trigger effect activated when spirits use their own skills, functioning as the core damage amplifier of the rotation, alongside a similarly-described "space/spatial domination" skill. a third guide (fori88.co.kr) gives korean names that partially resolve two of the naming conflicts above. it confirms 냉기충격 (literally "cold-air shock"), the left-click basic attack that increases attack power on hit and is used to fill cooldown windows kr-era single source fori88.co.kr, date unknown3. it also confirms 화염전소 (literally "flame complete-burn"), the right-click basic attack that provides a skill-speed increase and is alternated with the cold skill via a "left-right cancel" during filler time. based on the literal korean, "cold shock" is the more literal rendering of 냉기충격 and "flame incineration" (rather than "flame transfer") is the more literal rendering of 화염전소, since 전소 means "burned up completely" and gives no basis for a "transfer" translation. translation conflict, partially resolved: the confirmed kr names above show "cold shock" and "flame incineration" are the more literal english renderings of the two basic-attack skills, and "flame transfer" looks like a less literal translation of 화염전소 rather than a separate skill. "space domination" vs "spatial domination," and "corrosion" vs "curse" (used as a stigma name by one guide, a skill by the other), most likely still reflect different fan translations of the same korean text rather than different skills. still contested whether "cold shock" and "frost shock" name the same skill remains unresolved: a separate english-language search summary describes "cold shock" as a distinct signature skill providing the class's only lifesteal, and "frost shock" as a different secondary skill assigned to left and right click for maintaining debuffs, implying they are two separate skills rather than one skill under two fan names single source, exact url not isolated, from a websearch synthesis over multiple vortex gaming spiritmaster guides. no official global name has been found for either skill mmoculture.com, 2026-074. net: treat "cold shock" (via 냉기충격) as confirmed as a basic-attack skill; treat whether "frost shock" refers to the same skill or a different one as unresolved. no reliable source found for an explicit "avoid these skills" list. guide a's advice to skip wind spirit in the core 3-spirit rotation is the closest equivalent, but this is a pve efficiency choice, not a "bad skill." other sources recommend wind spirit specifically for escape/chase/disruption utility, so it is situational rather than universally skippable search-summary only, source 403'd exitlag.com, date unknown5. spiritmaster skill priority leveling active passive warala

title: Stigma picks
text: stigma picks stigmas unlock at 23 with 5 slots; pve favors pet output and dot uptime, pvp favors debilitation effects. stigmas unlock at level 23 with up to 5 slots after the march 25, 2026 kr patch (shared system fact) kr-era, balance may change aion2hub.com, 2026-031. that same patch added a new spiritmaster-specific stigma called "command: proxy," which reworks an existing skill named "kaisinel's power" into a party buff granting +20% status accuracy/resistance, alongside several spirit skills being converted into aoe effects aion2hub.com, 2026-032. early stigma order level "corrosion" and "fixed spirit" to rank 5 first then "spirit's grace" and "fixed spirit" again remaining slots from "shadow of curse," "flame blessing," or additional "corrosion" depending on preference single source, unconfirmed wording vortex gaming's guide independently lists stigma priorities as "blessing of fire" (accuracy/crit/damage amplification), "protection" (defensive spirit ability), "stabilization" (consistency), "corrosion" (debuff damage), and "blood drain" (an hp-based shield, called a strong defensive pick for hard content) vortexgaming.io, date unknown3. translation conflict: "corrosion" and "blessing of fire"/"flame blessing" appear across both guidance sets above, giving moderate (2-source) confidence to those two specifically, though naming again varies slightly between sources. pve vs pvp: aion2boost.com frames pve stigma priority as pet output and dot uptime first, control second; pvp priority as debilitation effects (fear/drain) first, then pet resilience/pressure, then survivability for extended trades aion2boost.com, 2026-084. summarized by that source as "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost." no reliable source found for a confirmed advanced stigma (level 45) list for spiritmaster specifically, or for a definitive "spend stigma shards on x first" recommendation beyond the general cross-class advice to fund frequently-used stigmas before spreading investment expcarry.com, 2026-095. spiritmaster stigma picks build slots

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route shared board system; raise main skill levels and take orange end-branch nodes before minor skill levels. shared system mechanics (see the sorcerer guide for the full node-color and board-unlock breakdown): board unlocks at level 12 (nezekan), with further boards at 20 (zikel), 30 (vaizel), 40 (triniel), and advanced boards at 45 (ariel for pve, azphel for pvp, plus marchutan and yustiel referenced in one source) fextralife.com, 2026-011. node types: grey = stats (1 point), green = passives (2 points), blue = active skills (3 points), orange = unique board-specialty bonuses (4 points), same source. for spiritmaster specifically, aion2boost.com's pve priority order (pet output and resilience first, dot uptime second, control third) implies favoring daevanion nodes that raise spirit-related active skills and their survivability stats before general caster stat nodes marketing source, inferential aion2boost.com, 2026-082. a kr skill-tree and combo guide gives an explicit spiritmaster daevanion priority order: raise skill levels on main abilities toward specific targets, levels 16 and 12 are commonly cited breakpoints, before taking orange end-branch nodes take orange end-branch nodes for damage amplification, cooldown reduction, combat speed, and crit-damage resistance take minor skill levels and multi-hit-related nodes last kr-era single source fori88.co.kr, date unknown3 this order is single-source and general within the class rather than tied to specific named nodes on the board, but it is the most concrete spiritmaster-specific daevanion guidance found so far. it broadly agrees with the general cross-class "prioritize active/blue nodes early" advice. spiritmaster daevanion board route nodes

title: Arcana
text: arcana essential spiritmaster arcana picks are spirit's majesty, corrosion, and inferno; treat exact names as provisional. arcana is a shared cross-class system (see the sorcerer guide for slot types, grades, and training arcana values) kr-era, balance may change expcarry.com, 2026-091. the general dps-class advice, prioritize cards raising levels on the active skills and passives driving your main rotation, then complete damage-oriented sets, applies to spiritmaster as a dps class, but the source gives no spiritmaster-specific card names or slot priorities. spiritmaster-specific picks (single kr guide) essential: spirit's majesty (survival and buff core), corrosion (dot and debuff application), inferno (flame damage output) optional but recommended: absorption (30 second cooldown, hp recovery, stable play), onslaught of ruin (60 second cooldown, high dps plus a groggy value of 50, described as less convenient to use) these are fan-translated names from a single kr guide, not confirmed official terms kr-era single source, fan-translated names fori88.co.kr, date unknown2. this card list is single-source and kr-era. treat exact card names as provisional until a second source or global localization confirms them; no spiritmaster-specific card slotting order beyond "essential vs optional" was found, and no source names cards to avoid. spiritmaster arcana cards transcendence

title: Gear and stat priority
text: gear and stat priority orb is the only weapon; magic attack, spirit efficiency, hp/defense, mana regen, and accuracy form the stat foundation. weapon: orb (confirmed across all sources). stat priority, per a pvp-build-focused guide: magic attack, spirit efficiency, hp/defense, mana regeneration, and accuracy "form the foundation" pvpbank.com, date unknown1. do first: a high-magic-attack orb with spell power, general advice for dps classes is to upgrade the weapon first then: hp for survivability, since the caster is a sustained-pressure class later / optional: mana regeneration and accuracy to round out the "foundation" stats detailed gear stat breakpoints from vortex gaming's pve build (single source, kr-era, terminology likely translation-specific): pursue "perfect" quality options on pants, cloaks, shoes, and gloves single source, numeric values unverifiable vortexgaming.io, date unknown2. prioritize attack power (cited around 258) and critical hit/accuracy (cited around 147) on stat rolls. for awakening (an enhancement tier) prioritize damage resistance, amplification, critical damage, and impact; for "magic stones" (the manastone/godstone-equivalent socket system), "weapon damage increase" is called the most efficient choice. for pvp, the same source recommends awakening priorities of hp, status effect resistance, iron wall, impact resistance, and damage resistance, plus a "pvp damage amplification" magic stone (advanced abyss variant) or "vitality" as an efficient alternative. vortexgaming.io claim describes spiritmaster in pvp as "a straightforward damage-trading class with no cc, movement skills, or slows." vortexgaming.io, date unknown3 other sources' documented kit document fear/root/knockback tools: soul's cry, ashy call, earth spirit bind, wind spirit knockback/silence. fextralife.com, 2026-024 pvpbank.com, date unknown5 contested: the "no cc, movement skills, or slows" claim is in clear tension with the fear/root/knockback kit documented by two other sources above. this looks like an error or an oversimplification in the vortexgaming.io pvp section rather than a genuine build difference. manastone/godstone-equivalent system (shared, general description in the sorcerer guide): sockets on gear, manastones for weapon/armor, spiritstones for accessories, godstones for extra combat effects, resettable via soul imprinting kr-era vortexgaming.io, date unknown6. no reliable source found for confirmed spiritmaster set-effect names. spiritmaster gear stat priority weapon orb

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos keep a spirit alive and buffed before you summon it; damage collapses the moment a spirit expires. core mechanic, confirmed across multiple sources: keeping spirits alive and actively rotated is "the single biggest factor in spiritmaster output," with damage falling off sharply once summons expire aion2hub.com, date unknown1. the "warala" rotation concept (single source, kr-derived term, spelling and translation not independently confirmed): rather than keeping one persistent spirit summoned, the class repeatedly re-summons spirits to retrigger on-summon effects (named "space/spatial domination" and "elemental fusion") frequently mmoexp.com, 2026-072. a 3-spirit rotation (fire, water, earth) is recommended over a 4-spirit rotation, since adding wind spirit is said to slow the cycle and reduce overall damage efficiency. beginner pve macro/rotation vortex gaming, single source, kr-era: keep the skill macro limited to one skill ("flame incineration"), and manually trigger "frost shock," "elemental fusion," "curse," and "spatial domination" via separate mouse buttons, pressing them continuously to maintain debuff uptime. cast a buff (translated "flame blessing") open with basic attacks after using "spirit's grace," summon "fixed spirit" at higher gear/skill levels, replace some summons with basic attacks; keep water spirit and re-summon it roughly every 15 seconds for its single-target damage vortexgaming.io, date unknown3 mmom.com, date unknown4 (corroborating the same general macro pattern) buff-before-summon timing rule (a specifically called-out beginner mistake): activate buffs such as "blessing of fire" and "protection" before summoning "ancient spirit," because spirits inherit the caster's current stat bonuses at the moment they are summoned. buffing after summoning wastes the effect for that spirit's lifetime mmoexp.com, 2026-075. pet/spirit management (confirmed, consistent across 3+ sources) fire spirit: offensive summon, applies a burning dot and reduces enemy defense (one detailed source cites 150 damage/sec and a 30% defense reduction, single-source numeric figure) fextralife.com, 2026-026 water spirit: healing, cleansing, and shields (same source cites 370 hp per 3 seconds, single-source figure), described elsewhere as the class's primary sustain tool during long fights gamesolusi.com, 2026-077 earth spirit: gives a damage-reduction shield and can knock down/bind enemies, called "one of the most complete tank pets" wind spirit: knocks back and silences, boosts the caster's own movement speed, functioning as the class's escape/chase/disruption tool fextralife.com, 2026-028 pvpbank.com, date unknown9 combo/utility skill: "command: substitution" causes the active spirit to absorb 100% of the caster's incoming damage within a 15-meter radius for 30 seconds, described as a major defensive cooldown that can be paired with a "spirit sacrifice" effect for large defensive or offensive payoff fextralife.com, 2026-0210 pvpbank.com, date unknown11. situational spirit pairings recommended by one source (single source, contested against the "3-spirit warala" advice above, which specifically favors fire/water/earth): pve sustain = earth + water; pvp control = fire + wind; solo farming efficiency = fire + earth contested pvpbank.com, date unknown12. no reliable, verified source found for a documented dedicated "auto-hunt" skill setup separate from the manual macro descriptions above. spiritmaster rotation combos spirits warala macro

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes one of the strongest solo classes: the spirit tanks for you, and it wins fights through attrition, not burst. solo leveling comfort is rated as strong: spiritmaster is repeatedly described as "one of the strongest solo classes," with the spirit acting as a built-in frontline/tank so the caster is not the sole damage sponge aion2hub.com, date unknown1 aion2boost.com, 2026-082 (describing "solo safety via personal frontline"). sustain is comparatively good thanks to water spirit's healing/cleanse and siphon's lifesteal, though damage output is explicitly tied to keeping a spirit alive and correctly positioned, so sustain and damage both collapse together if spirit uptime lapses aion2hub.com, date unknown3 fextralife.com, 2026-024. no reliable source found with spiritmaster-specific pull-size guidance. general framing from aion2boost.com is that the class wins fights through attrition rather than burst, so players should "embrace attrition pacing" rather than expect quick single-cast kills aion2boost.com, 2026-085. when the class "turns on": sources agree the class becomes meaningfully stronger once the player has internalized spirit-cycle management, summon timing, buff-before-summon sequencing, and elemental fusion triggers, rather than at a specific level breakpoint. no reliable source ties this to an exact level number. spiritmaster leveling notes solo mob density

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes most mistakes come from letting a spirit die, buffing too late, or under-investing in pet-facing nodes. treating spiritmaster as a "simple pet class" and being overwhelmed once the actual rotation depth (spirit cycling, not button-mashing) becomes apparent mmoexp.com, 2026-071 letting spirits die before re-summoning instead of summoning preemptively to maintain continuous uptime mmoexp.com, 2026-072 buffing after summoning "ancient spirit" instead of before, since the spirit inherits the caster's buffs only at the moment of summoning mmoexp.com, 2026-073 wasting spirits by summoning them outside the effective combat area, or summoning right before a forced reset/phase change mmoexp.com, 2026-074 adding a fourth spirit (wind) to the core pve rotation when a tighter 3-spirit cycle is reportedly more damage-efficient contested, wind is also recommended for pvp/escape mmoexp.com, 2026-075 ignoring positioning relative to your own spirit, losing access to spirit-granted shields/heals that require proximity pvpbank.com, date unknown6 spamming fear/cc on cooldown instead of using it to lock a specific threat at the right moment, "fear locks opponents strategically, not spam" pvpbank.com, date unknown7 assuming pet damage alone carries fights in high-end pve without accounting for boss movement disrupting spirit positioning, which several sources flag as the class's biggest competitive-pve weakness allthings.how, 2026-088 underinvesting in pet-facing stigma/daevanion nodes in favor of caster-facing ones, when the framing is that "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost" aion2boost.com, 2026-089 spiritmaster common mistakes pve pvp spirit uptime
