title: Overview and role
text: overview and role cleric is a near-mandatory pure healer: tanky, solo-friendly, but its tier likely dropped after a kr/tw patch. version note: aion 2 has been live in kr/tw since november 2025. global pc launch is october 5, 2026, with a fully wiped launch scale test on september 17-18 that does not carry over. most cleric guides below are kr/tw-era. a reported august 2026 balance patch cut fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, reportedly pushing cleric toward c-tier single source leprestore, date unknown1. treat any older "s-tier healer" claim as stale. role and kit cleric wields a mace paired with a shield or magic offhand ("guard") for a tankier build, with a staff option for higher magic boost and more damage oneall forum, date unknown2. aion2 hub describes it as a back-line healer who cycles aoe and over-time heals plus protective shields to sustain the group aion2hub, date unknown3. only class that can actively dispel debuffs, and carries the signature summon resurrection skill, making it near-mandatory for dungeon groups confirmed, multiple sources aion2hub, date unknown4 fextralife, date unknown5 fextralife calls it "an indispensable character in party play," but says it specializes in aoe healing over single-target: "the cleric's healing alone will not be enough" if the party ignores mechanics fextralife, date unknown6 standing by mode party demand: very high, near-mandatory for dungeons and raids pve: strong utility pick from its heal, shield, cleanse and res kit, though the august 2026 patch reportedly weakened fixed healing passives marketing source leprestore, date unknown7 pvp: viable as a "survival healer" build, but reportedly slipped to c-tier alongside chanter after the same patch single source leprestore, date unknown8 solo: good. fextralife calls it "accessible for solo players"; other guides call it tanky and safe to solo, kill speed aside, thanks to self-sustain from its own healing kit fextralife, date unknown9 mmoexp, date unknown10 beginner tip: pick cleric if you want a forgiving, hard-to-kill class with guaranteed group invites and don't mind managing cooldown rhythm and positioning over raw damage numbers. cleric overview role healer identity

title: Skill priority
text: skill priority keep a heal and a damage skill both leveled; the exact global-launch order is unconfirmed, so treat lists below as directional. gap: no reliable source found for a precise, level-by-level global-launch skill point order. the lists below are pieced together from kr/tw-era guides and should be treated as directional, not exact. do first: keep 1-2 healing skills (healing light / light of regeneration) leveled alongside your main damage chain. a cleric with no heal rank is unplayable in groups, and one with no damage rank kills too slowly solo (synthesized from the sources below). do first: below level 20, spec divine retribution 2 and 4 to leverage the spirit synergy vortexgaming, date unknown1 then (pve, level 20+): divine retribution (2/3/4), judgment bolt (2/4/5), sacred energy (3/4/5), light of regeneration (1/4/5), troops (2/3/4) vortexgaming, date unknown2 sacred energy is a higher dps priority; troops hits max dps with a full charge. then (pvp): shift light of regeneration to 1/2/5 (defense over mobility), troops to 3/4 (full-charge windows are rarer in pvp), and shock release to 1/4 or 1/5 at level 16+ vortexgaming, date unknown3 later / optional: a separate arcana-tied guide orders leveling as forge first (highest dps), then swift heal, earth's retribution, rain of healing, troops, and lightning judgment vortexgaming, date unknown4 that guide suggests reducing light of regeneration below level 16 to free points. two guides, two orders vortex gaming skill-tree guide divine retribution, judgment bolt, sacred energy, light of regeneration, troops as the level 20+ pve core vortexgaming, date unknown5 vortex gaming arcana-tied guide forge, swift heal, earth's retribution, rain of healing, troops, lightning judgment, with light of regeneration deprioritized early vortexgaming, date unknown6 these two guides partially conflict on light of regeneration's priority; treat as contested, not confirmed. named kits aion2 hub names the offensive kit as earth's retribution, judgment thunder, and divine punishment, and the healing kit as light of regeneration, healing light, and radiant recovery (the grouping is this guide's; the source lists the skills without grouping them) aion2hub, date unknown7. playstyle: weaving damage skills between healing cycles to maintain mana efficiency. a basic solo leveling loop cited elsewhere is applying punishment seal, spamming holy strike, and healing as needed marketing, lower trust. cleric skill priority leveling sp

title: Leveling build
text: leveling build push earth's retribution and heavenly judgment first, keep divine grace and earth's blessing maxed, then take divine burst as your first stigma. this order comes from the one inven post that frames leveling by skill-level band, cross-checked against an aggregated early-priority search summary inven 408, 2025-111. every "lv" figure below is the skill's own level (its 8/12/16/20 spec breakpoints), not your character level, confirmed by a dcinside thread discussing a stigma at "level 15" while still leveling dcinside, date unknown2. skill point order stepwhenskilltake towhysrc 1from lv 1earth's retribution (대지의 응보)skill lv 12 (1/3 pick)core auto-attack-cancel partner skillinven 408, 2025-11 2nextcondemnation (단죄)skill lv 8first skill taken in this bandinven 408, 2025-11 3nextlightning bolt (벽력)skill lv 12secondary damage, priority is contested (see note)inven 408, 2025-11 4nextchain of suffering (고통의 연쇄) and weakening mark (약화의 낙인)skill lv 12 eachstarts the paired resistance-debuff uptimeinven 408, 2025-11 5nextheavenly judgment (심판의 번개)skill lv 16 (2/5 pick)the single most important breakpoint in the rotationinven 408, 2025-11 inven 105, 2026-01 6nexthealing light (치유의 빛)skill lv 16 onlytriggers heavenly judgment's bonus hit; do not push further yetinven 408, 2025-11 inven 19538, 2026-05 7nextblessed radiance (쾌유의 광휘)skill lv 16its spec tier once both heals are at 16inven 408, 2025-11 two sources disagree on lightning bolt's priority: the leveling-era inven post treats it as a lv 12 pick, while a post-cap vortex gaming writeup calls it near-essential only at lv 20, after a patch made full-charge use mandatory inven 408, 2025-113 vortexgaming, date unknown4. this looks patch-driven, not a real contradiction: follow the lighter lv 12 investment while leveling, save the heavier push for after a similar patch lands globally. the note gives no separate "leave at level 1" list; the closest equivalent is capping warm blessing and healing power enhancement at 1-2 spare points below instead of leveling them properly. passives first: divine grace (주신의 은총), master it first, a flat attack-power passive needed for solo hunting efficiency inven 105, 2026-015 then: earth's blessing (대지의 은총), master alongside divine grace for additional attack power single source later: warm blessing (따뜻한 가호) and healing power enhancement (치유력 강화), only 1-2 spare points each while leveling; see the rotation and combos card below keep divine grace and earth's blessing maxed for hunting speed; see passives above single source lv 12nezekan daevanion board opens cooldown-reduction nodes (2.5% x2), combat-speed nodes (2.5% x2), and active-skill nodes first inven 72, 2025-118 passive order: healing power enhancement, then earth's blessing, then divine grace grey stat nodes in order: attack power, hp, defense, crit lv 23stigma: divine burst first, then absolution (targets are stigma levels; title: Stigma picks
text: stigma picks level earth's punishment to 20 first; beyond that, two guides disagree on names, and unlock-level claims are single-source. what stigmas are stigmas are advanced skills separate from your leveling tree, funded with stigma shards instead of skill points, equipped in a limited number of slots (6 in the kr-era cap) expcarry, date unknown1. a general aion 2 stigma-system explainer: complete a level-20 campaign quest to begin using stigma stones single source boostroom, date unknown2 slots open automatically at further level thresholds. this source is written specifically about aion 2, not the original aion, though it doesn't caveat kr-versus-global differences. a weaker, korean community signal says two additional advanced stigma slots open at level 45. this is a slot-count claim only, and the source thread could not be isolated, so treat it as unconfirmed single source, weakly sourced level 45 advanced stigma list (korean cleric board) a korean cleric-board thread on 상급스티그마 선택 (advanced stigma selection) recommends this set, all to level 25 unless noted single source kr-era inven, date unknown3: 대지의징벌 (earth's punishment) 보호의빛 (protection's light) 고결한기운 (noble energy), scales better for damage at levels 20-25 than amplified prayer 증폭의기도 (amplified prayer), to level 23 only, whose main benefit is a 1.5-second duration increase two guides, different names two guides give different core stigma lists for the same class; treat this section as contested in naming even though the general shape (pve = group sustain, pvp = personal survival) agrees. guide a (vortex gaming, via search summary) pve: light of protection (15), earth punishment (20), amplification prayer (15, fixed), ruin (15), summon resurrection (5), salvation (15, situational) single source pvp: exemption (15), salvation (15), yustiel (15-20, fixed), summon resurrection (5), ruin (15), earth punishment (20, situational) guide b (vortex gaming, direct fetch) pve "core four": power of life, earth's punishment, noble aura, light of possession vortexgaming, date unknown4 dungeon add-ons: salvation for hall of illusions (grouped laser pattern survivability); salvation + power of uriel for sanctuary pvp party: summoned hatchling, power of uriel, power of life/absolution, light of possession pvp solo: light of possession, power of uriel, noble aura, power of life, salvation both guides agree earth's punishment leveled to 20 is a near-universal pick, and that pvp swaps in more personal-survival stigmas (salvation, power of uriel/yustiel) versus pve's group-sustain focus. naming differences like "light of protection" vs "power of life" may be translation or patch-version drift rather than confirmed distinct skills contested. a korean-language community summary (titles found via search, not directly fetched, single source) lists these party-heal stigmas, covering cleanse, defense/attack buffs, resistance buffs, and move-speed boosts: 면죄 (exemption/absolution) 치유의 기운 (healing energy) 보호의 빛 (light of protection) 유스티엘의 권능 (power of yustiel) beginner tip: spend stigma shards first on stigmas already equipped in your main rotation before funding alternates, and pick ones that unlock a specialization effect at a reachable level over spreading thin expcarry, date unknown5. cleric stigma picks pve pvp

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route build one full rotation on mastery skills first, then fund the daevanion nodes that support it; no cleric-specific route is confirmed. the daevanion board is a node-investment system spent with daevanion points, gated by character level. this is a general system note, not cleric-specific expcarry, date unknown1. lv 12nezekan board unlocksstart spending daevanion points. lv 20zikel board unlocks lv 30vaizel board unlocks lv 40triniel board unlocks lv 45four advanced boards unlockariel, azphel, marchutan, yustiel. node costs and route node cost tiers (general system): grey (stat) 1 point, green (passive skill) 2 points, blue (active skill) 3 points, orange (unique skill) 4 points single source aggregation recommended early route, not cleric-exclusive: prioritize blue (active skill) nodes early for immediate combat power for a healer specifically: prioritize your main damage chain skill and any node that boosts an hp-recovery skill or a skill usable while moving gap: no reliable source found for a cleric-specific, node-by-node daevanion route naming actual nodes on any board. resets individual nodes or the whole board can reportedly be reset, at a kr-era cost of about 500 kinah per node, explicitly flagged as "subject to change on global" expcarry, date unknown2. general guidance: build one full rotation on mastery skills first, fund the stigmas used in that rotation, trace the cheapest daevanion path that supports the same build, and only reset when your role changes meaningfully. daevanion points and crystals come from leveling/quests, achievements, and content activities expcarry, date unknown3. cleric daevanion board progression

title: Arcana
text: arcana fill chalice with damage/heal skills, prioritize divine grace on bell and healing power boost on mirror, and lock old cards instead of deleting them. card types arcana cards come in types referenced as chalice, bell, mirror, and scales vortexgaming, date unknown1: chalice: aim for 2+ of these skills on one card - forge, swift heal, earth's retribution, rain of healing, troops, lightning judgment vortexgaming, date unknown2 bell: priority order is divine grace (minimum level 3), then shield of immortality, then warm aura mirror: priority is healing power boost first (target level 4), then earth's blessing second (target level 3), which improves critical-damage scaling scales: get at least 2 useful active skills on the card since it "heavily influences your overall setup direction" a separate ai-summarized search result for the same underlying guide family gives a near-identical bell/mirror/scales list, cross-confirming the above. setup and cost strategy when synthesizing chalice cards, check 2 roll options if affordable; for other card types, 1 option is enough to save resources. for general bonus sets, favor "frenzy 4 pure" or "history 4 pure" over "vitality," since vitality cards are expensive and not worth chasing unless already owned. avoid: deleting old arcana cards when the meta shifts. lock them instead, since balance patches can bring old cards back into relevance. don't sink heavy resources into vitality-type cards from scratch vortexgaming, date unknown3. gap: no reliable source found confirming whether "chalice, bell, mirror, scales" are the actual global localization terms or a fan/kr-guide translation. treat the names as provisional pending global client confirmation. cleric arcana chalice bell mirror scales

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos solo, apply punishment seal and spam holy strike; in a party, cycle heals and shields proactively rather than firefighting damage. solo pve loop apply punishment seal. spam holy strike as your main damage filler. heal as needed rather than on a fixed timer. earth's retribution and judgment thunder let cleric chip in meaningful ranged damage and sustain its own mana while healing aion2hub, date unknown1. party and support rhythm cleric does not spam heals constantly; it follows a rhythm confirmed, qualitative: cycling aoe and over-time heals, layering shields proactively, and cleansing debuffs rather than firefighting single-target damage. fextralife: the cleric specializes in area of effect healing rather than single-target support, and gameplay is bouncing between different healing sources while weaving in damaging skills fextralife, date unknown2. many heals (e.g. healing light) can be charged for a stronger effect at the cost of higher mp and cast time. beginner tip: use shield skills like immortal curtain (absorbs a fixed amount for up to 10 seconds per fextralife) proactively before a known boss mechanic hits, not reactively after damage lands. macro layout suggested layout: charge on q, all three healing skills bound together on num 1, instant attack skills on num 2, stigma skills spread across num 5-8 keyran, date unknown3. the same source cautions that most veteran players keep healing and buff macros manual rather than fully macroed, since heal/buff timing precision matters more than raw damage-chain speed. gap: no reliable source found for a confirmed auto-hunt skill setup specific to cleric. cleric rotation combos macro

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes cleric levels safely and comfortably solo thanks to self-healing, but kills slower than true dps classes. solo leveling comfort rates positively across sources: cleric is "tanky and safe to play solo" and, unlike a stereotypical helpless solo healer, has enough offensive tools to handle solo content while maintaining excellent sustain marketing, lower trust u4n, date unknown1. its self-heal (e.g. healing light) means less time on potions or downtime between fights. kill speed is slower than true dps classes; the tradeoff is durability and near-zero death risk while leveling. gap: no reliable source found with specific pull-size or mob-density numbers for cleric, and none identifying a specific level or gear milestone where cleric's power spikes. general guides only say the class stays viable and safe throughout leveling. cleric leveling notes solo sustain

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes stay active and mobile: shield before damage lands, swap stigmas by content, and don't lean on burst heals to fix mechanics. do apply offensive pressure during downtime instead of only reacting to damage mmoexp, date unknown1 call out repositioning so aoe heals land on a grouped party use shields proactively before a known burst ("immortal curtain is proactive, not reactive") balance skill points between damage and healing kits rather than dumping into one swap stigma loadouts by content (pve party, pve solo, pvp), per korean community guidance ("don't stick to one setup, must swap by content") lock old arcana cards instead of deleting them when the meta shifts vortexgaming, date unknown2 stay mobile while healing to dodge avoidable boss/pvp attacks do not play as a purely passive, reactive healer mmoexp, date unknown3 heal when nobody needs it, wasting mp and triggering long cooldowns early in a fight assume aoe heals land when the party is spread out too far rely on burst single-target healing to fix every mechanic mistake, "the cleric's healing alone will not be enough" fextralife, date unknown4 use shields reactively after damage already landed stand still while healing instead of staying mobile cleric common mistakes beginner errors

title: Overview and role
text: overview and role chanter is a melee support/healer hybrid, strong in groups but its unique value is wasted playing solo. version note: aion 2 has been live in kr/tw since november 2025. global pc launch is october 5, 2026, with a fully wiped launch scale test on september 17-18. nearly all chanter guides below are kr/tw-era. a reported august 2026 balance patch removed fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, which one source says dropped chanter to c-tier alongside cleric single source leprestore, date unknown1. possibly aion 1: some search results for this class returned original-aion fan wiki pages (aion.fandom.com, differ.blog, an aspirine.su stigma calculator) rather than aion 2 sources. those are excluded from claims below except where explicitly flagged as a conflation risk. role and kit chanter is a hybrid support/melee class. aion2 hub calls it a "staff-wielding hybrid priest who buffs, heals, and fights on the front line" aion2hub, date unknown2. fextralife similarly describes it as a hybrid support that increases ally stats during party play and can function in several roles simultaneously, from buffer to a secondary healer or damage dealer fextralife, date unknown3. weapon: staff. unlike the original aion, chanter can now block effectively with the staff itself, removing the old mace-and-shield swap so staff is the single weapon for offense and defense single source. identity aion2 hub frames it precisely: chanter is "never the main healer, yet able to keep a group standing while contributing real damage," trading peak healing output for survivability and offense, a "sustain-and-support bruiser" aion2hub, date unknown4. fextralife notes a mechanical limitation: the class lacks instant single-target heals but excels with aoe regeneration zones, and cites beta feedback calling it "a hybrid healer with high dps and strong self-sustain" fextralife, date unknown5. difficulty, demand, and solo play difficulty and grade: one build-guide site rates chanter medium difficulty, pve grade b, pvp grade b single source aion2boost, date unknown6 caveat: "its grade is a function of your roster, not just your hands," over-performing in premades and merely hitting its stated b tier in solo queue. party demand: called "the clear top choice if your priority is party buffs." single source aggregation runs a mantra-based toolkit with offensive, defensive, and utility benefits. the build most players will expect for group content like dungeons, rift battles, world bosses, and guild raids. this contrasts with cleric's more universal, role-agnostic demand. solo viability is contested between sources. fextralife says chanter is "great for soloing due to high dps and healing ability" with strong self-healing and survivability when playing solo fextralife, date unknown7 other aggregated guides describe a "control bruiser" that thrives in solo play with fast mob clearing thanks to built-in sustain and crowd control marketing, lower trust aion2boost.com is more skeptical: solo viability is "modest as a standalone bruiser" because the class struggles without allies to benefit from its buffs, making solo play less rewarding than group content aion2boost, date unknown8 net read: chanter solos fine numerically, but its unique value is wasted when alone. beginner tip: pick chanter if you enjoy melee-range hybrid support and expect to run with a regular static group or guild. aion2boost.com's verdict: "pick the chanter if you play with regular groups; avoid it if exclusively solo queueing." chanter overview role support hybrid

title: Skill priority

crushing wave is useful for both macro chains and animation canceling vortexgaming, date unknown1. then: level huyu's spell to 16 (10% max hp recovery, 3-second cast-time reduction) vortexgaming, date unknown2 level gust dance to 16 (on-hit, reduces all skill recast time by 1 second). level heat wave strike to 16 (a successful block gives 25% chance to reset its recast time). then: prioritize charge strike's 5-second recast reduction spec (it triggers heat wave strike on a successful hit). prioritize crushing blow's hp-drain spec for survivability. prioritize vibration blow's range spec paired with the raging blow combo for bosses. later / optional: striking blow as a combo filler for boss fights (its stun does not apply to bosses). an gyeok se as an aoe skill paired with the penetrating blow combo for trash. shock release specced for 20% hp recovery on cast, noted as "limited effectiveness in certain dungeons." two guides' passive order guide 1 passive order first priority: attack preparation, cocoon's spell, blessing of life ("increases health and healing amplification"), will to survive, promise of wind, spell of path second priority: cross protection, promise of earth, shock hit vortexgaming, date unknown3 guide 2 passive order first-priority: attack preparation, blessing of life second-tier: impact hit, inspiration spell third priority: promise of earth, promise of wind single source attack preparation and blessing of life are consistently top priority across both guides; the rest of the ordering is contested. because chanter's healing kit is aoe regen zones rather than instant burst heal, guides suggest leveling hand of recovery / huyu's spell alongside your main damage chain (dark wave, crushing wave) rather than one before the other, since group-sustain and "real damage" are both core to the class per aion2 hub's description aion2hub, date unknown4. gap: no reliable source found for a precise level-by-level sp order for global launch, or a single unambiguous "ignore this skill early" list beyond the low-priority passives noted above. chanter skill priority leveling sp passives

title: Daevanion board route
text: daevanion board route put early daevanion points into max mana and wave strike nodes; the board system itself is shared across all classes. the general daevanion system (board names, node color/cost tiers) is shared across classes: nezekan (lvl 12), zikel (lvl 20), vaizel (lvl 30), triniel (lvl 40) boards, plus four level-45 advanced boards. grey/green/blue/orange nodes cost 1/2/3/4 points respectively. no reliable source found suggesting this system differs for chanter; see the cleric write-up for the general mechanics. lv 12nezekan board unlocks lv 20zikel board unlocks lv 30vaizel board unlocks lv 40triniel board unlocks lv 45four advanced boards unlockariel, azphel, marchutan, yustiel. chanter-specific guidance from one source: "concentrate investments primarily in max mana and wave strike nodes. select damage resistance nodes (ariel, aspel) if avoiding pvp content" single source vortexgaming, date unknown1. this implies a stat-node (max mana) plus active-skill-node (wave strike, likely tied to the dark wave/crushing wave chain) route early, with ariel and azphel recommended for pve-focused players seeking damage resistance over pvp-oriented boards. gap: no reliable source found for a full node-by-node early route, when to reset, or which of the four level-45 advanced boards is best for a pvp-leaning chanter specifically. chanter daevanion board progression mana

title: Gear and stat priority
text: gear and stat priority battle chanter goes critical hit and physical attack; support chanter goes for buff uptime and survivability over raw damage. weapon: staff, used for both offense and, per one source, an in-class block mechanic, removing the need for a shield swap. do first (offensive / "battle chanter"): critical hit and physical attack for damage per hit and faster mob clearing, plus critical hit and accuracy so crowd-control effects land reliably single source aggregation. then (support chanter): gear that "enhances your support toolkit" over top-tier dps stats, since "your value comes from survivability and consistent buff uptime." later / optional: a note of uncertain provenance for aion 2 suggests magic boost is only a secondary stat for chanter, since the class is fundamentally physical low confidence, possible aion 1 conflation possibly carried over from original-aion guidance. physical attack, critical hit, and attack speed are the suggested primary stats. aion2boost.com's build philosophy: "uptime matters most, a weaker buff maintained consistently outperforms a stronger one that lapses," implying cooldown reduction and buff-duration stats should be weighed alongside raw damage stats for a support-oriented chanter aion2boost, date unknown1. gap: no reliable source found for which specific gear piece to enhance first for chanter, nor for named set-effect gear pieces (unlike cleric, no player-submitted example build page was found). no reliable source found for a manastone/godstone-equivalent socketing system specific to chanter. chanter gear stat priority weapon staff

title: Rotation and combos
text: rotation and combos rotation names are contested across guides; the constant is mantra upkeep, recast them immediately after every death. solo pve rotation (aggregated guide, lower trust) engage with cc. apply strike chain for guaranteed stun and damage over time. cleave with ascendant strike. drop a regen zone for sustain. repeat the rotation. naming conflict: these skill names (strike chain, ascendant strike) do not match the dark wave/crushing wave/back breaker names from the vortex skill-tree guides, likely reflecting different translation passes or patch versions rather than confirmed distinct skill lists. treat exact skill names as provisional. a second phrasing closer to aion2 hub's own description: open with staff combos including onslaught, resonance crush, impactful crush, and crushing blow to apply physical damage and debuffs, while "life-leech and stat-boosting mantras" maintain party viability aion2hub, date unknown1. again this skill-name set does not overlap cleanly with the vortex guide's names. animation canceling combo single source: "crushing wave and then use a skill based on left-click or source of recovery" is cited as a rapid-execution animation-cancel sequence; the guide itself stresses this reflects "personal opinion and not the definitive answer" vortexgaming, date unknown2. mantra and party rhythm mantra/aura upkeep moderate confidence, single source: chanter's signature mechanic is the mantra system, buffs that are instantly cast, persist until manually cancelled or replaced (not on a timer, and "cannot be dispelled by any means"), and act as an aura benefiting the whole nearby group by proximity. up to three mantras can be active solo, or four if grouped with a second chanter. this may partly describe original-aion mantra mechanics carried into aion 2. party composition should steer mantra choice: a caster-heavy party benefits from magic-boosting mantras, a melee-heavy party benefits from physical attack power/critical rate mantras. beginner tip: always recast mantras immediately after death/respawn, since they drop and are not automatically restored. gap: no reliable source found with a named chanter defensive cooldown analogous to cleric's immortal curtain, or a confirmed auto-hunt skill setup for chanter. chanter rotation combos mantra

title: Leveling notes
text: leveling notes chanter levels solo just fine numerically, but its buffing identity only shows up in a group. solo leveling comfort is generally rated positively for raw survival and clear speed, "fast mob clearing and excellent sustainability" thanks to built-in sustain and crowd control marketing, lower trust. but aion2boost.com's more skeptical framing should be weighed against this: chanter's identity is built around buffing others, so solo leveling, while numerically fine, does not showcase the class's actual strength and may feel comparatively flat next to classes fully usable alone aion2boost, date unknown1. sustain: regen zones plus life-leech mantras give consistent self-sustain without heavy potion use, similar in spirit to cleric's self-healing but delivered as an aoe zone rather than an instant heal. this means chanter benefits from standing in its own zone rather than kiting constantly (inferred from fextralife's "lacks instant single-target heals but excels with aoe regeneration zones" note, moderate confidence). "turns on" point: aion2boost.com's grading suggests chanter turns on specifically when joining an organized/premade group rather than at any particular character level or gear milestone; its value is structurally tied to having allies present to buff. gap: no reliable source found for a specific level or cp number where chanter's personal (non-buff) power spikes, beyond the single korean-community note that roughly 2200 combat power is enough to function as a main-healer substitute in easier content. no reliable source found for specific mob-density or pulling-size comfort numbers. chanter leveling notes solo sustain

title: Common mistakes
text: common mistakes fight in melee range with your group, keep mantras up, and never play chanter like a ranged cleric. do stay in melee range, fight with your group, and amplify everyone around you pvpbank, date unknown1 pre-place aoe healing/regeneration zones where the team is stacked recast mantras every time after respawning play close to the tank, you are strongest in the center of the fight prioritize survivability first, damage second, a dead chanter provides no buffs to anyone keep a weaker buff up consistently rather than chase a marginally stronger one that lapses (aion2boost.com's build philosophy) recognize the class's grade is roster-dependent, lean into premade/organized groups do not play chanter like a cleric, standing at range and healing pvpbank, date unknown2 spam direct heals instead of placing healing zones forget to recast mantras after dying stay too far from the tank/fight prioritize personal damage over survivability and buff uptime chase mantra swaps so aggressively that uptime drops neglect the hand of recovery / huyu's spell recovery line while over-investing in the damage chain, undermining the "never the main healer, yet able to keep a group standing" identity chanter common mistakes beginner errors

title: How to read the badges
text: how to read the badges each badge shows how much agreement backs a claim, not how important that claim is. every fact-bearing card, bullet, or table row in this guide carries one of these badges next to it. they describe how much agreement exists behind a claim, not how important the claim is. confirmed two or more independent sources agree on this. still not official, but it is not one guide's guess either. single source only one write-up documents this. could be right, could be a translation slip or a one-off patch quirk. treat as a starting point, not gospel. contested two or more sources give different numbers, names, or rankings for the same thing. both versions are usually shown so you can judge for yourself. kr-era this number or mechanic comes from the korean or taiwanese live client. global launches with different tuning, sometimes very different (see the monetization walk-back after the kr launch backlash), so treat kr-era numbers as directional, not final. official traced back to ncsoft, plaync, the nc newsroom, or an official steam/store listing rather than a fan translation. marketing comes from a boosting, carry, or gold-selling site. these sites write a lot of the detailed guide content in this space (there simply isn't much else pre-launch), so their factual claims are used when nothing better exists, but any framing that nudges toward "buy this service" is not neutral advice. beginner tip: if a card only carries single source or marketing badges, read it as "plausible, worth trying, don't panic if the live game disagrees." badges confidence trust legend how to read

title: Known unknowns to re-verify after 2026-10-05 launch
text: known unknowns to re-verify after 2026-10-05 launch nothing below is confirmed for global launch; re-check every number once founder access opens. avoid: treating any number on this page as final. everything below was flagged in the research itself as unverified, single-source, contested between sources, or simply missing. re-check each one against the live global client once founder access opens september 30, 2026. general global character level cap at launch is contested. lv 45: the original kr/tw cap. lv 50: a kr-updated cap. lv 20: a separate active-skill and stigma enhancement cap mentioned for global. this figure comes from one lower-trust source. single source mmoexp, oct 20261 daevanion board count is contested; this exact disagreement recurs in nearly every section that touches daevanion. contested 6 boards per one wiki page: nezekan 12, zikel 20, vaizel 30, triniel 40, ariel 45, azphel 45. 8 boards elsewhere, adding marchutan and yustiel at level 45. fextralife2 daily and weekly reset times for global servers were not published anywhere found; every reset time in this guide (daily 05:00, weekly wednesday 05:00) is a kr/tw server time and may not match a given region's server. kr-era aion2kina.com3 the full, itemized list of all nine weekly checklist activities was never found; only daily items were documented in detail anywhere. whether na/sa/eu/asia region servers will have separate faction population balancing or queues at global launch: not found. the kr "chapter 1" mentor system (circle tokens / orichalcum tokens, membership event pass) is kr-era patch content; it may not exist at global launch on day one. kr-era daeva's report4 no official aion2.plaync.com page, no steam community hub, and no massivelyop.com kr-launch article (http 403) were directly read for this research; the kr launch-controversy narrative rests on search-engine summaries of blocked pages plus secondary coverage. systems stigma unlock and slot progression is contested: one source says a single slot unlocks at level 23 with up to 4 equipped; another gives a detailed 23 / 30 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 ladder ending in a major stigma slot. contested aion nova5 vs aion2hub6 kr raised the stigma level cap from 20 to 25 with a higher-tier shard; whether this cap applies at global launch is explicitly unconfirmed. kr-era expcarry7 arcana rarity item-level bonuses (common +20 / rare +40 / epic +60 / unique +80) versus a competing "green 40 / blue 60 / unique 80" naming scheme for what looks like the same tiers. contested expcarry8 equipment grade naming is inconsistent across sources and not resolved into one scheme. contested official patch notes reportedly confirm heroic and unique. one community source adds rare/unique/legendary tiers from different content. a separate green/blue/purple/gold scheme is used for pantheon items. the pantheon system (statues, colossi, deity domains) rests on a small cluster of sources (mainly one aggregator plus a boosting site) with no wiki or database confirmation found anywhere. single source vortex gaming9 achievement totals: 1,307 (one database) versus 4,225 total / 2,685 reward-granting (a different snapshot or counting method). contested aion2hub10 whether aion 2 has a traditional class-advancement or ascension tier at all: no evidence found. "awakening battles" exist as a separate timed solo-challenge track, not a class upgrade. whether a dyeing system exists: no evidence found either way; flagged unverified rather than confirmed absent, since classic aion had one. manastone/godstone-equivalent socketing ("engraving" reroll mechanic, soul binding "growing once bound") comes from a single fan-run compiled wiki and is not corroborated elsewhere. single source aion 2 kodex11 the "atul" name for the combat power score, and the stat soft-caps quoted for it (accuracy 1700 / crit 80%), come from one boosting-adjacent guide and may be a translation artifact. single source u4n12 monetization whether founder's pack tier upgrades (standard to a higher tier) are purple-only and unavailable on steam: single source, not corroborated. lagofast.com13 nc's own membership announcement leaves "additional gameplay benefits" officially vague. confirmed: market access, the kina-quna exchange, and the kina shop. unconfirmed by nc itself: claims of extra storage or "enhanced progression". single source u4n14 no published xp-rate bonus, drop-rate bonus, energy refill, auto-hunt duration, or exact inventory-slot count tied to membership was found anywhere. daeva pass premium track price in usd or quna: not found in any source checked. whether daeva pass "upgrade materials" (nc's own wording) actually affect gear power: nc has not clarified this either way; editorial coverage calls it the most ambiguous purchase in the whole monetization stack. contested mmorpg.com editorial15 whether kr-era combat-boosting cash-shop items are permanently banned from ever reappearing in the west is unconfirmed. items in question: combat enhancement scrolls, soul book items. not confirmed in nc's own words, only consistent with nc's current "cosmetics and consumables only" framing. a claimed 60-day steam funds hold and a 14-day/under-2-hour refund window are both single-source and not verified against steam's or nc's actual policy text. single source eur-specific founder's pack or membership pricing: not found published separately from the usd figures used throughout this guide. dungeons and energy the energy resource's own name is contested: "odell," "odyle," "odile," and "aetherine" energy all appear to be different fan translations of the same korean term (오드 에너지). contested energy regen rate: one source cites 15 per 3 hours, but a second (unfetchable, relayed via snippet) implies that figure already includes a +50% membership bonus, meaning the real base rate could be closer to 10 per 3 hours. contested u4n16 the "1,400 energy per week" total and its breakdown come from a single korean source that itself returned http 403 on direct fetch; it is the lowest-confidence numeric figure used anywhere in this guide. single source game.savetip.co.kr, 202517 the 560-energy cap itself is kr-era and unverified for global; whether it is a hard cap or a weekly-accumulation figure is unclear. kr-era expedition party size is directly contested: 4-player per older teasers, 5-player per newer steam materials, and 8-player per a separate wiki naming specific elyos/asmodian expeditions. contested weekly entry-limit counts conflict throughout: expeditions cited as 3/week, 21/week, or "0/3 limit" depending on the source; transcendence cited as 2/week or 14/week. contested fortress sieges are directly contested, worth flagging prominently. contested one source (fetch blocked, search-summary only) claims large-scale sieges are returning. a second, directly-fetched source explicitly states original-aion-style sieges are not confirmed for aion 2. timesaver.gg18 whether a "fatigue" system that reduces xp gain over time exists: only speculative, conditional language found ("if implemented"); no concrete mechanic or numbers documented. no beginner-facing gank-avoidance mechanics (safe zones, pvp flagging grace periods for new characters) were documented anywhere; treated as a genuine gap. "region missions" and "tower/challenge modes" as named systems: neither was confirmed to exist under those names; both may only appear in korean sources that returned http 403 on every fetch attempt (namu.wiki, inven.co.kr). essentially every specific number in the dungeons/energy topic is kr-era and pending reconfirmation at launch. kr-era no official nc global patch notes were retrieved. no official aion2 site content was retrieved. no steam community numbers were retrieved. templar no reliable source found for templar-specific stigma picks, a daevanion node route, a specific gear-enhancement order, a ranked passive list, or an auto-hunt/macro setup. every other class section found at least partial answers to these; templar did not. skill count: 31 active/10 passive per one hub page versus 43 total (33 active/9 passive) per a separate guide. contested two competing arcana set recommendations (vigor 4/purity 4 vs a vigor/magic/purity mix), both single-source with no direct fetchable article. the "sword-vs-mace depends on stigma type, weapon before armor" advice found in search results traces back to the original 2009 aion's fan wiki, not aion 2; flagged as legacy-game information rather than presented as fact. gladiator total skill count agrees at 52, but the active/passive split is contested: 43 active/9 passive versus 40 active/9 passive from the same domain on different fetches. contested two vortex gaming guides give partly conflicting pve skill priority orders and partly conflicting pve/pvp stigma sets for the same class. contested pre-release focus-group feedback calling the class "slow and clunky" versus later framing that it "transforms" mid-game: both may be true at different patches, but this is pre-launch feedback that balance passes may have already addressed. contested named gear-set pieces (nua, gunyongwang, "rin sword," a crafted "garder" belt) come from one kr-era guide and may not map 1:1 to eventual global localization. single source no gladiator-specific daevanion node route was found anywhere. assassin pve standing is contested: "best pve class for clearing content" per one class-guide source versus a tier list arguing assassin gains more from short pvp bursts than sustained boss damage. contested skill/stigma naming is inconsistent across guides: "heart gore" / "heart stab" / "heart," and "illusive clone" / "illusion clone" / "phantom clone" likely all describe the same skills under different fan translations. contested a korean inven thread gives a contested "pattern-first vs heart-first" combo ordering, resolved differently depending on whether mastery investment is complete. single source inven (kr)19 the assassin field manual's specific arcana card-to-skill assignments and manastone enhancement order are single-source, from one fan-made site not independently corroborated. ranger pve ranking is contested: "second-best pve class, just behind assassin" per one source versus "only slightly lower than elementalist and sorcerer" per a tier list. contested pvp tier is contested: "a-tier, cleanest roaming pick after assassin" versus "a stable b-tier pick." contested rupture arrow priority directly conflicts between two guides: one deprioritizes it as "less effective for total dps," another says a balance patch "significantly increased" its utility. contested no reliable source found for a ranger passive-skill order, a clean pve-vs-pvp stigma split, specific arcana card assignments, a manastone-equivalent enhancement order, or which gear slot to enhance first. the claim of "11 active skills, 13 stigma skills, 5 equippable at once" comes from a single video title/description only; the video's actual content was never retrieved. single source sorcerer pve grade is sharply contested: a-tier "with a real claim on higher" per one build-guide source versus c-tier per a leaderboard-data tier list that found only 83 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots were sorcerers. contested allthings.how20 skill names are inconsistent and machine-translated across guides: firebomb/firestorm/blaze/ice chain in one source versus cool down/fire spell/hellfire/ice break/wisdom of lumiere in another, describing what looks like the same core kit. contested no single authoritative skill-leveling order using confirmed global skill names was found anywhere. no sorcerer-specific arcana card names or slotting order were found; general dps-class advice was applied by extension only. global stigma slot cap is unconfirmed; kr raised it to 5 slots and expanded the level cap to 25 in a march 25, 2026 patch, but whether that carries to global is unstated. kr-era spiritmaster pve grade is a three-way contest. contested c-tier per one build-guide source. d-tier, the lowest of any class (only 34 of 800 leaderboard slots), per a leaderboard-data tier list. allthings.how21 a-tier, "biggest winner of pre-launch balance passes," per a third source that itself returned http 403 on direct fetch and is unverified against its own original text. two guides give different english names for what appears to be the same core mechanics: "cold shock" vs "frost shock," "flame transfer" vs "flame incineration," "corrosion" vs "curse." contested one source frames spiritmaster pvp as having "no cc, movement, or slows," which directly contradicts the fear/root/knockback tools (soul's cry, earth spirit bind, wind spirit knockback) documented in multiple other sources for the same class. contested the "warala" rotation term is single-source and its spelling/translation from korean is unconfirmed. single source cleric exact stigma unlock level for cleric specifically is unconfirmed; the commonly assumed level 23 is a general system figure, not independently verified for this class. two vortex gaming guides give different core stigma name lists for what is likely the same skills under different translation passes (light of protection vs power of life, amplification prayer vs noble aura). contested no cleric-specific, node-by-node daevanion route was found; no manastone/godstone-equivalent socket details were found for this class specifically. arcana card-type names (chalice, bell, mirror, scales) are not confirmed as actual global localization terms versus a fan/kr-guide translation. single source no reliable source found for a specific level or gear milestone title: Research method
text: research method this guide is built from search and page fetches, not hands-on play, and treats kr/tw numbers as directional, not final. this guide was compiled on september 12, 2026, roughly three weeks before global launch, using web search and page fetches rather than hands-on play, since the global client does not exist yet. topics were researched separately: the general overview, systems, monetization, and dungeons/energy topics, and one per class. every claim is linked inline and badged by confidence. method search for recent aion 2 coverage on the target topic. fetch the most promising pages directly. fall back to search-engine result snippets when a fetch failed (a large number did, mostly http 403 from boosting and vpn-marketing sites that block automated readers). every claim was tagged at the point of writing as confirmed, single source, or contested, based on how many independent sources agreed. it was separately flagged kr-era whenever a number could only be traced to the korean or taiwanese live client rather than an official global statement. the kr/tw-versus-global gap the single biggest limitation running through this entire guide is the kr/tw-versus-global gap. aion 2 has been live in korea and taiwan since november 2025, so almost every specific number here, from skill breakpoints to dungeon entry limits to stigma slot counts, was measured on that client. global launches october 5, 2026 with its own balance pass (nc has already announced changes like no heroic-gear drops and different item-level gates), so treat every kr-era number as a reasonable starting guess, not a locked-in fact. no fact in this guide was invented to fill a gap. where research genuinely turned up nothing, the relevant card says "no reliable source found" rather than guessing, and those gaps are collected in the known unknowns card above so they are easy to re-check once founder access opens on september 30, 2026 and the client is actually in players' hands. citation reliability: a random sample of 20 sourced sentences was re-checked against the linked pages; 15 were fully supported, 1 partially (correct skill names, grouping added by this guide), and 3 pointed at a page that did not carry the claim. assume a residual error rate of roughly one in seven chips: click through before acting on any specific number. korean-language sources korean-language community sources (inven.co.kr, namu.wiki, dcinside, fmkorea, arca.live) were targeted deliberately, since kr/tw players have a ten-month head start on every mechanic in this game. most direct fetches of those sites returned http 403. where their content shows up here at all, it is relayed through an english-language guide that cites them, or through a search-engine snippet, never a verified direct read. research method methodology how compiled web search

title: Glossary
text: glossary mastery skill your class's core combat ability, learned automatically at level requirements and raised with skill points up to a base cap of 10. expcarry, date unknown1 specialization chosen bonus effects a skill gains at level breakpoints 8, 12, and 16, up to 3 extra effects per skill. fextralife, date unknown2 empyrean trace / feather a world collectible turned in at a monolith for wisdom stones. naming is inconsistent between sources, possibly different translations of the same kr item. fextralife, date unknown3 differ, date unknown4 wisdom stone a consumable obtained by exchanging empyrean traces/feathers at a monolith, grants skill points on use. fextralife, date unknown5 stigma an equippable skill-enhancement stone adding build-defining abilities on top of your class kit. first slot unlocks around level 23. expcarry, date unknown6 stigma shard the currency spent to level a stigma skill, separate from normal skill points. higher-tier shards exist for kr levels 21-25. expcarry, date unknown7 daevanion board a permanent node-board progression system, separate from gear, raising combat stats and effective skill levels. first board unlocks at level 12. fextralife, date unknown8 daevanion point spent to unlock individual daevanion board nodes; earned from regional quests, sealed dungeons, strongholds, achievements, and exploration. overgear, date unknown9 daevanion crystal earned alongside daevanion points from the same sources, also obtainable via material conversion; feeds daevanion board progression. expcarry, date unknown10 arcana a card-based system adding item level, combat stats, set bonuses, and effective skill levels at once. slots include chalice, parchment, compass, bell, and mirror, later expanded. expcarry, date unknown11 training arcana a consumable that feeds experience to arcana cards; tiers are lesser (200 exp), intermediate (600), superior (1,500), and ultimate (3,000). expcarry, date unknown12 mana stone a socketed gem added to gear for stats like crit rate or speed, found via dungeons, rewards, or crafting; aion 2's manastone equivalent. u4n, date unknown13 soul codex alongside mana stones, described as helping gear "scale into late-game without major farming" by increasing attribute effects. fextralife, date unknown14 soul binding a secondary stat block on gear that reportedly "only grows once you bind it." single-source, unverified. kodex.yavuz, date unknown15 theostone a weapon proc stone, aion 2's godstone equivalent, socketed into a weapon's dedicated slot for a chance-on-hit effect. one effect per weapon; identical theostones do not stack. 153 known theostones cataloged. aion2.online, date unknown16 enhance stone spent to raise a gear piece's enhancement level. extraction from a previously-enhanced item refunds 100% of the enhance stones spent into it. exitlag, date unknown17 broker aion 2's player marketplace/auction house; kinah is the only currency usable there. fextralife, date unknown18 pantheon a permanent passive-stat system built from statues, colossi, and "artwork"; placing a colossus grants points toward a deity domain, each capping at 200 points before converting to flat combat stats. vortex gaming, date unknown19 colossus a pantheon item slotted to grant domain points; its rarity (green/blue/purple/gold) determines bonus strength. rsnxt, date unknown20 achievement points granted by completing achievements; ties into daevanion point/crystal income. differ, date unknown21 title an earned label from pvp rank, arena tiers, boss kills, monster-hunting milestones, or events; stat titles grant bonuses like pvp attack or hp when equipped, some are purely cosmetic. aion2hub, date unknown22 appearance collection a wardrobe-style collection; roughly 700 appearances grants combat speed and cooldown reduction as a milestone bonus. cash-shop cosmetics do not count toward it. vortex gaming, date unknown23 soul (pets/mounts) a monster drop; farming 10 souls of almost any monster unlocks it as a pet/mount. also drops from the shugo shop and black cloud merchant. fextralife, date unknown24 flight power a wing's airborne stamina stat, managed via a physics-based "glide gauge" rather than a rigid timer. thegamer, date unknown25 glide gauge the physics-based mechanic underlying flight power; running it out mid-air drops you. u4n, date unknown26 legion aion 2's guild system, capped at up to 128 members, used for pve, pvp, crafting, and social access. 6sword, date unknown27 legion hall unlocks at legion level 5, costs 1,000,000 kinah to rent, houses all five crafting professions' merchants/workbenches together. mmoexp, date unknown28 legion coin earned for active legion contribution; spent on legion-exclusive skins, uniforms, masks, mounts, and wings. u4n, date unknown29 accuracy governs the chance to land an attack; per one source, also affects crit chance. u4n, date unknown30 precision a hybrid stat that raises both accuracy and crit chance. u4n, date unknown31 pve attack / defense comes only from pve gear; only affects damage dealt to and taken from monsters. exitlag, date unknown32 pvp attack / defense comes only from pvp gear; only affects damage dealt to and taken from other players. exitlag, date unknown33 item level a gating number for content access, cited around 900-2700+ tiers for transcendence content. fextralife, date unknown34 combat power ("atul") an aggregate power estimate used for matchmaking/ranking-style comparisons. the "atul" name is single-source and may be a translation artifact. u4n, date unknown35 transcendence aion 2's endgame progression/ranking layer, fed by specific dungeons with up to 4 escalating difficulty levels. aion2hub, 2026-0736 odyle energy spent to open the reward cube after clearing an expedition or transcendence dungeon; entry itself is not gated by energy. normal cube costs 40, hard costs 60. aion2hub, 2026-0737 essence extraction the gathering skill/action used to mine ore, gather herbs, or cut wood, feeding all five crafting professions. expcarry, date unknown38 kinah the main in-game currency; earned from quests, monster kills, dungeons, and vendor sales, spent on repairs, soul-binding, crafting materials, teleports, and gear enhancement, the only currency usable on the broker. u4n, date unknown39 quna the premium/cash-shop currency, obtained mainly via real-money purchase and tradeable for kinah through a currency exchange, spent on cosmetics and battle pass premium tiers. u4n, date unknown40 abyss points earned from daily/weekly pvp-zone quests; presumed to buy abyss-specific gear/items, not independently confirmed. fextralife, date unknown41 centuryroot token spent at a "shugo festival" seasonal shop; purpose beyond that event unverified. fextralife, date unknown42 glossary terms currencies systems jargon

text: glossary additions style shop the referenced but unnamed source of post-creation appearance changes; a special currency or cash-shop item is needed to alter your look after character creation finishes, exact item not yet named for global. fextralife, date unknown1 rune (accessory) an accessory-slot item distinct from manastones, theostones, and arcana cards. named examples: clash rune, devotion rune. two good runes are worth roughly 80 item levels. fextralife, date unknown2 kodex.yavuz, date unknown3 transfer crafting a single-source crafting process that carries a gear piece's enhancement, amplification, and soul binding progress into its next-tier upgrade, guaranteed to succeed, resulting item becomes soul bound. unconfirmed by a second source. kodex.yavuz, date unknown4 legion hideout rentable legion space, only an officer can rent it, costing 1,000,000 kinah for 23 days and 15 hours. distinct from the disputed "legion hall" claim in the legion card on the systems page. guildmanager.app, date unknown5 abyss rank (trainee through supreme commander) a 20-tier seasonal pvp ranking ladder built on abyss points. ninth-class soldier needs 3,000 points; the single supreme commander slot needs 25,000,000. kr/tw server data. aion2hub, date unknown6 pet genus insight / possession effect a mechanic where leveling and collecting pets grants passive combat power, separate from simply riding a pet as a mount. vortex gaming, date unknown7 odella a high-tier gathering material (about 6 per gathering session) used to craft "odella energy," a daevanion crystal-equivalent material, plus higher-tier wings and equipment. possibly the same underlying resource as this guide's "odyle energy," unconfirmed. vortex gaming, date unknown8 inder boss a boss encountered while gathering, defeating it is tied to odella yield. vortex gaming, date unknown9 glossary terms missing systems jargon
